http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m02-002.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:19]
Re: Oddity In Chandler & Buran's Rendlesham

  Cabansag admits he sat in Halt's office and signed a statement
  without reading it. Burroughs denies ever having a lighthouse
  chase.
  Reportedly the Bentwaters base commander Col. Ted Conrad
  initiated an inquiry and interviewed Penniston, perhaps others,
  the very next day, Dec. 27, 1980, despite the Christmas holiday.
  Lt Col Halt was Conrad's subordinate, as deputy base commander.
  It seems unlikely that Conrad and Halt who had to work together
  closely would undertake separate investigations without
  coordinating with each other. Penniston reportedly was next
  interviewed by AFOSI right after Conrad, on Dec. 27 (Bruni p.
  177).
  It seems most likely that the 81st Security Police police-
   witness statements were prepared for both base commander Conrad
  and his deputy Halt. The fact that Halt seems to have kept
  copies and later reportedly made copies available to CAUS does
  not mean that others such as his immediate superior Col. Conrad
  had no copies. Since SP and AFOSI work closely together any
  statements made for Conrad and Halt would have been subject to
  almost unavoidable AFOSI influences on SP witnesses.
  One cannot assume that Halt was immune to AFOSI pressures. One
  possibility is that he was told that he could release the
  witness statements only if they included _all_ of the
  statements, including the sugar-coated poison pill statements
  backing up the (false) "lighthouse chase" that would make Halt
  look bad. Naturally Halt was in no hurry to release such a
  boobytrapped collection.
  AFOSI has a track history going back to 1949 of planting and/or
  spreading fictitious stories of crashed saucers, alien body
  recoveries and/or meetings of AF officials with live aliens. How
  long will we continue to let ourselves be fooled by these absurd
  disinformation ploys? With Rendlesham, AFOSI merely recycled and
  replanted its bogus story of the Holloman AFB landing where AF
  officials met the aliens and helped them with spare parts. The
  Holloman disinfo had been planted on Sandler and Emenegger in
  1972. Eight years later it resurfaces at Rendlesham, with only
  the date and location changed. Are we that frikkin stupid that
  we can't see a pattern here??
  Here's hoping for a smarter New Year.

  Brad

  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>

  Subject: One Last Look Back



  Source: Billy Cox's Blog | De Void
  http://tinyurl.com/26mrnd
  Monday, Dec. 31, 2007 at 5:37 p.m.

  One Last Look Back
  By Billy Cox
  billy.cox.nul
  De Void's First Annual Year in Review:
  Biggest honkin' sighting: British commercial airline pilot Ray
  Bowyer reported seeing two UFOs, one approximately a mile wide,
  over the Channel Islands on April 23. Passengers and a French
  pilot confirmed the encounter.
  Most ignored news: The National Aviation Reporting Center on
  Anomalous Phenomena's 152-page analysis of the UFO that buzzed
  Chicago's O'Hare airport in 2006. NARCAP's scientists
  discredited the FAA's "weather phenomenon" explanation, but
  their conclusions received no media coverage. That's because the
  report came out on July 27, the same day the riveting Paris
  Hilton told Larry King, "Even though (jail) was really hard, I
  took that time just to get to know myself."
  Fourth Estate Award: To freelance journalist Leslie Kean.
  Working with the Coalition for Freedom of Information, Kean in
  March coaxed former Arizona governor Fife Symington to go on the
  record with his own sighting of the so-called "Phoenix Lights"
  UFO in 1997. In November, she convinced a federal court to order
  NASA to review its files (again) for documents pertaining to the
  1965 Kecksburg Incident. A few days later, Kean and filmmaker
  James Fox assembled an international panel of pilots urging the
  U.S. to renew its official UFO research.
  Biggest waste of airtime: CBS Sunday Morning's Aug. 12 cupcake.
  Normally the best show on commercial television, the network's
  bovine approach employed tired Hollywood themes to reach an
  Earth-rocking conclusion: "For now, the most definitive UFO
  sightings remain at the movies, where aliens are not shy about
  making themselves known."
  Biggest 'visionary' cop-out: In November, CNN Senior Vice
  President/youth-demographic hustler David Bohrman told Wired
  magazine it would be a mistake to allow its Web page visitors to
  decide which YouTube questions to submit to the presidential
  candidates. Because that would've meant, given the high volume

One Last Look Back

  Biggest surprise of the year: UFOs finally made it to the
  campaign trail, albeit to a chorus of chortling. Picking up on
  MacLaine's contention that her longtime buddy Dennis Kucinich
  saw a UFO at her residence, NBC's Tim Russert elicited a prime-
  time confession from the long-shot Democrat on October 30. As a
  result, half a dozen other presidential candidates, Dems and
  Republicans, proclaimed themselves UFO skeptics.
  Best subsequent one-liner: Mike Huckabee, Nov. 4 =97 "I believe in
  G-O-D, not UFO."
  Mr. Tenacity: Winnipeg's Grant Cameron. Veteran researcher's
  FOIAs have produced letters and photos linking Bill and Hillary
  Clinton to UFO disclosure advocate Laurance Rockefeller.
  Curiously, conspicuously, Republicans have refrained from using
  these revelations to attack the Clintons.
  Weeniest editorial: Flaccid, equivocating Dec. 1 opinion by the
  Los Angeles Times on how the coverage of Kucinich's UFO sighting
  "put the issue back on the radar." The Times actually described
  calls for the declassification of UFO data as "reasonable", then
  proceeded to back away from the subject with cheeky references
  to men in black and the "cult of the UFO". It went on: "Kucinich
  mentioned in his own defense that President Carter was a UFO
  witness, and he might have mentioned that Ronald Reagan was as
  well. Then again, if you think presidents really run the
  country, well, that's what 'they' want you to think."
  So here's to 2008, with hopes for a little more coherence and a
  firmer resolve to explore the unmapped road.

  by individuals and organisations, and the reporter has kept a

  >Dark Materials".
  >---
  >A staple of mind-bending science fiction, the possibility of
  >multiple universes has long intrigued hard-nosed physicists,
  >mathematicians and cosmologists too.
  <snip>

  G'day all:
  One thing I always find intriguing about discussions of parallel
  universes, multiverses, bubble universes and the like, is the
  extreme nonchalance demonstrated in the use of the term
  'infinite'. Infinity is a terribly weird thing: you can add
  infinity to it without increasing it, delete infinity from it
  without decreasing it, and so on.
  Furthermore, as is often commented, in an infinite world
  (whether in size or duration) anything with a possibility higher
  than zero will necessarily occur (and indeed - this point is
  often missed - because infinity is equal to infinity times
  infinity, will happen an infinite number of times).
  This allows a huge array of strange arguments to be made. Thus,
  a theist could argue that, if the possibility of an omnipotent
  god existing is less than zero, and it should be unless there is
  something contradictory about the concept, then an omnipotent
  god (or an infinite number of them) would necessarily exist.
  Further, as it is omnipotent, this god would have the ability to
  interact with all the universes, and therefore it is necessarily
  the case that a god (God?) does exist in this universe!
  Countless other such arguments could be produced.
  One that may be of interest to Ufology at large, and which is
  discussed by physicists, is the appearance of the strange
  'Boltzmann Brains' - sentient beings which simply 'pop' into
  existence, and which some cosmologists fear may actually
  outnumber biological intelligences such as ourselves, thus


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m02-009.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:23]
Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

  threatening our 'typical observer' status. See:
  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boltzmann_brain
  and:
  http://tinyurl.com/2sca6s
  I wonder what impact the possibility of such beings should have
  on the 'evolution of human-like intelligence' discussion?

  Sincerely,
  James T. Molesworth

  By 3TV Staff

  >visitors.

  G'day Ed.
  Forgive me, but I find your argument a little confusing. If
  'tool-making' is what 'sets us apart' from other animals, surely
  it cannot also be convergent, as this requires precisely that we
  are _not_ set apart by this ability, but share it with other
  species. Indeed, this also requires that tool making not be
  perceived as a 'niche' (for that matter, I fail to see why
  'intelligence' should needs be a niche, as Lineweaver contends,
  as it is surely itself a potential adaptation suitable to a
  range of purposes and hence survival techniques).
  Furthermore, on what evidence can it be claimed that 'certain
  physical and mental traits will follow' from tool making? It c
  ould very well be argued that the reverse is true.
  I'm afraid I must humbly disagree and contend that it is indeed
  aspects of our intelligence that makes humans unique among
  terrestrial species - the ability to develop, communicate and
  comprehend highly complicated and abstract concepts, among other
  features, may be regarded as the reason why our utilisation and
  manufacturing of tools differs markedly in extent and complexity
  from that of other species, and indeed not just physical tools,
  but also conceptual tools such as numbers, and attendant symbols
  of diverse types. Importantly, this is why Lineweaver was
  careful to use the term 'Human-like Intelligence' rather than
  just 'intelligence', for various other species do display
  intelligences of varying types and extent, but there appears to
  be a significant difference in kind between the conceptual
  abilities of these and that of humans.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m02-011.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:24]
Re: 'Why Would ET Evolve Human-Like Intelligence?'

  That said, I should point out that I am no advocate of
  Lineweaver's conclusions. I am pleased that a discussion of the
  topic appeared in a mainstream scientific publication, and that
  it was treated seriously. I feel also that Lineweaver has
  highlighted a genuine point to consider, but ultimately the
  evolution of 'human-like intelligence' is a process for which we
  simply do not have enough data to form any firm conclusions.
  Certainly it should not be taken for granted, as it sadly often
  is, that an intelligence similar to that of humans will always
  evolve where the opportunity exists, any more than any other
  trait possessed by any species on this planet. On the other
  hand, it _may_ well be a feature of natural selection that it
  does tend to eventually precipitate the type of intelligence
  possessed by humans - educated guesses are the extent of our
  ability to answer such questions at this time, at least until
  other examples of evolutionary systems are discovered (assuming
  that such does occur).
  As something of an agnostic concerning the ET hypothesis, I
  should say that I regard as far more troubling the apparent
  physiological congruencies between such entities as the 'greys'
  and humans. Despite the fact that many reports tend to suggest
  they neither breathe, nor have a bony internal skeleton, and may
  not even eat or drink as we do, we nonetheless find that most
  reports describe beings far more externally similar to humans
  than could reasonably be expected from beings both
  evolutionarily entirely divorced from humanity, but also
  possessing (apparently) such widely different requirements from
  their bodies. Can the (apparent) internal differences between
  humans and the ETs have had no impact on the development of
  their gross external structure?
  One reply to this, of course, is that terrestrial life was
  'seeded' or somehow manipulated by an ET civilisation, and hence
  the similarities are a result of this. However, such does not
  explain why the similarities seem to end with the basic
  anthropomorphic appearance of the ETs, while their internal
  physiology seems (from what little information we have) to
  differ markedly. Further, how do such claims for the external
  'seeding' of Earth correlate with the argument that life has
  evolved independently throughout the universe?
  This then raises another problem - we simply do not know how
  life got started (assertions in popular literature aside), and
  hence cannot by any means know how likely or otherwise it is
  that life exists elsewhere. The discovery (assuming, as seems
  likely, that it takes place) that there are many Earth-like
  planets is double edged, for while it may be regarded as
  increasing the chances of life elsewhere, it may also be seen as
  allowing the possibility that the emergence of life was far more
  unlikely than previously appreciated, and required not only
  millions of years, but billions of potential loci to occur. The
  number of life-friendly planets may be astronomical, but so too
  may be the chances of evolution ever getting underway - we
  simply do not know.
  But, I am playing devil's advocate, and my intention is
  merely to indicate that the ET hypothesis should not be taken
  as an entirely unproblematic, 'obvious' explanation for the
  numerous UFOlogical phenomena.

  Sincerely,
  James T. Molesworth

  01 Jan 2008
  Oooh Arrrr Not Alone Anymore
  By John Coles
  j.coles.nul-sun.co.uk
  [Large Image]
  This stunning photo of a UFO over Cornwall was last night hailed
  by experts as one of the best ever taken in Britain.
  The classic flying saucer shape is seen above two ships.
  And UFO watchers believe it could be proof we are not alone.
  Kelvin Barbery snapped the mystery object from a coastal path
  between Swanpool and Maenporth, near Falmouth.
  In a weird twist, Kelvin, 55, did not even see the UFO at the
  time.
  He thought he was just taking a sea view =97 but when he loaded
  the digital camera card on to his computer, the round metallic
  'craft' was in the centre of the shot, about two miles away.
  Kelvin, a facilities manager for schools, said: "There were a
  couple of tankers out in the bay and I thought that it made a
  nice shot.
  "There was nothing in view and certainly no fault on the camera.
  When I got home I couldn't believe what I had. I thought, 'Wow,
  where did that come from?' I'm not the sort to believe in UFOs =97
  now I'm not so sure."
  Nick Pope, one of Britain's foremost UFO experts, said the photo
  was one of the best he had seen.
  Nick, formerly the official Ministry of Defence UFO analyst,
  said: "If I was still there I'd be looking at this very closely.
  The object looks structured, symmetrical and metallic. This man
  has caught something very interesting indeed."
  Michael Soper, of the Contact International UFO group, agreed:
  "This does appear genuine. Digital photos can be doctored but
  everything about it appears consistent."
  ---
  Kelvin took his picture at 3.31pm on December 29, with a Nikon
  D80 Digital SLR on automatic.

  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>

  Archived: Wed, 02 Jan 2008 09:54:24 -0500
  Subject: UFOs Or Too Much Revelry?



  Source: The San Diego Union Tribune - California, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/2gxacl
  January 1, 2008

  New Year's Eve Lights: UFOs Or Too Much Revelry?
  by Susan Shroder
  It was New Year's Eve, after all, and people may be in altered
  states where they see lots of strange things.
  But three groups of San Diegans swear they were sober enough to
  report seeing strange orange-yellow lights in the sky about 30
  minutes after midnight. And the National UFO Reporting Center
  said Tuesday it got enough "similar reports from across the
  country" to warrant a follow-up investigation.
  Ryan Keegan and his wife, Rachael, were leaving a friend's party
  at their apartment complex in Bay Park about 12:30 a.m. when
  they saw the unidentified objects. They went in and got their
  friends and took pictures with a cell-phone camera.
  "We saw four orange lights in a square and right behind there
  were three orange lights in a triangle," said Keegan, who is in
  the home-financing business and whose wife is a kindergarten
  teacher. "There was no sound, no flashing lights, no vapor
  trail, just solid lights."
  They continued to watch the sky and Keegan said the group saw
  four more lights appear about 12:45 a.m. The lights traveled
  east to west, then disappeared in the sky over La Jolla.
  Keegan said he and his friends had been drinking, "but we
  weren't drunk being that it was Near Year's."
  About the time same in Pacific Beach, Dustin Gannon, an amateur
  astronomer, said he and about a dozen friends saw the lights
  from the backyard of his home. Gannon described them as nine red
  dots that traveled across the sky for about seven minutes. About
  a half-hour later, the group saw four red dots. They captured
  the images on video.
  "We're still a little freaked out," he said. "It was really
  crazy. It wasn't fireworks."
  Reached at the National UFO Reporting Center in Harrington,
  Wash., about 50 miles west of Spokane, center director Peter B.
  Davenport said a woman he knows in the UFO field made a similar
  report. She and five people saw the lights traveling in
  formation heading west toward Del Mar. She described it as one
  single unit with seven lights in total followed by an orange
  triangle formation; both disappeared into the marine layer over
  the ocean.
  "Based on the fact that I actually know the witness who


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m02-019.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:28]
UFOs Or Too Much Revelry?

  submitted this report, and based on the other seemingly similar
  reports from across the country last night, I would categorize
  this sighting over San Diego as of interest to us," Davenport
  said.
  San Diego police said Tuesday they did not receive any calls
  about New Year's Eve UFO sightings.
  The National UFO Reporting Center also received reports of
  similar sightings in Santa Monica, the San Francisco Bay area
  and Canada.

                                                       They're Made Out Of Meat
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Thu, 03 Jan 2008 06:48:05 -0500
  Archived: Thu, 03 Jan 2008 06:48:05 -0500
  Subject: They're Made Out Of Meat



  Source: Terry Bisson's Webite - Brooklyn, New York, USA
  http://www.terrybisson.com/meat.html
  March 13, 2003

  From OMNI, April 1991. This story, which was a 1991 Nebula
  nominee, has been appearing around the internet lately without
  my name attached. Several people were kind enough to alert me,
  but the truth is I'm more flattered than offended.
  ---
  They're Made Out Of Meat
  by Terry Bisson
  "They're made out of meat."
  "Meat?"
  "Meat. They're made out of meat."
  "Meat?"
  "There's no doubt about it. We picked up several from different
  parts of the planet, took them aboard our recon vessels, and
  probed them all the way through. They're completely meat."
  "That's impossible. What about the radio signals? The messages
  to the stars?"
  "They use the radio waves to talk, but the signals don't come
  from them. The signals come from machines."
  "So who made the machines? That's who we want to contact."
  "They made the machines. That's what I'm trying to tell you.
  Meat made the machines."
  "That's ridiculous. How can meat make a machine? You're asking
  me to believe in sentient meat."
  "I'm not asking you, I'm telling you. These creatures are the
  only sentient race in that sector and they're made out of meat."
  "Maybe they're like the orfolei. You know, a carbon-based
  intelligence that goes through a meat stage."
  "Nope. They're born meat and they die meat. We studied them for
  several of their life spans, which didn't take long. Do you have
  any idea what's the life span of meat?"
  "Spare me. Okay, maybe they're only part meat. You know, like
  the weddilei. A meat head with an electron plasma brain inside."
  "Nope. We thought of that, since they do have meat heads, like


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m03-001.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:29]
They're Made Out Of Meat

  the weddilei. But I told you, we probed them. They're meat all
  the way through."
  "No brain?"
  "Oh, there's a brain all right. It's just that the brain is made
  out of meat! That's what I've been trying to tell you."
  "So ... what does the thinking?"
  "You're not understanding, are you? You're refusing to deal with
  what I'm telling you. The brain does the thinking. The meat."
  "Thinking meat! You're asking me to believe in thinking meat!"
  "Yes, thinking meat! Conscious meat! Loving meat. Dreaming meat.
  The meat is the whole deal! Are you beginning to get the
  picture or do I have to start all over?"
  "Omigod. You're serious then. They're made out of meat."
  "Thank you. Finally. Yes. They are indeed made out of meat. And
  they've been trying to get in touch with us for almost a hundred
  of their years."
  "Omigod. So what does this meat have in mind?"
  "First it wants to talk to us. Then I imagine it wants to
  explore the Universe, contact other sentiences, swap ideas and
  information. The usual."
  "We're supposed to talk to meat."
  "That's the idea. That's the message they're sending out by
  radio. 'Hello. Anyone out there. Anybody home.' That sort of
  thing."
  "They actually do talk, then. They use words, ideas, concepts?"
  "Oh, yes. Except they do it with meat."
  "I thought you just told me they used radio."
  "They do, but what do you think is on the radio? Meat sounds.
  You know how when you slap or flap meat, it makes a noise? They
  talk by flapping their meat at each other. They can even sing by
  squirting air through their meat."
  "Omigod. Singing meat. This is altogether too much. So what do
  you advise?"
  "Officially or unofficially?"
  "Both."
  "Officially, we are required to contact, welcome and log in any
  and all sentient races or multibeings in this quadrant of the
  Universe, without prejudice, fear or favor. Unofficially, I
  advise that we erase the records and forget the whole thing."
  "I was hoping you would say that."
  "It seems harsh, but there is a limit. Do we really want to make
  contact with meat?"
  "I agree one hundred percent. What's there to say? 'Hello, meat.
  How's it going?' But will this work? How many planets are we
  dealing with here?"
  "Just one. They can travel to other planets in special meat
  containers, but they can't live on them. And being meat, they
  can only travel through C space. Which limits them to the speed
  of light and makes the possibility of their ever making contact
  pretty slim. Infinitesimal, in fact."
  "So we just pretend there's no one home in the Universe."
  "That's it."
  "Cruel. But you said it yourself, who wants to meet meat? And
  the ones who have been aboard our vessels, the ones you probed?


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m03-001.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:29]
They're Made Out Of Meat

  You're sure they won't remember?"
  "They'll be considered crackpots if they do. We went into their
  heads and smoothed out their meat so that we're just a dream to
  them."
  "A dream to meat! How strangely appropriate, that we should be
  meat's dream."
  "And we marked the entire sector unoccupied."
  "Good. Agreed, officially and unofficially. Case closed. Any
  others? Anyone interesting on that side of the galaxy?"
  "Yes, a rather shy but sweet hydrogen core cluster intelligence
  in a class nine star in G445 zone. Was in contact two galactic
  rotations ago, wants to be friendly again."
  "They always come around."
  "And why not? Imagine how unbearably, how unutterably cold the
  Universe would be if one were all alone ..."

  the end

Witnesses Describe Kucinich's Close Encounter




                                                          UFO Updates
                                    A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                                'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 3

                                        Witnesses Describe Kucinich's Close Encounter
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Thu, 03 Jan 2008 06:57:03 -0500
  Archived: Thu, 03 Jan 2008 06:57:03 -0500
  Subject: Witnesses Describe Kucinich's Close Encounter



  Source: The Wall Street Journal
  http://tinyurl.com/2t6w5j
  January 2, 2008;
  Page A1

  What Kucinich Saw: Witnesses Describe His Close Encounter
  Candidate's Pals Recall Three Throbbing UFOs;
  Outed by Shirley MacLaine
  By Michael M. Phillips
  michael.phillips.nul

  The 2008 presidential race has raised many questions about the
  candidates' personal histories. Will Barack Obama's past drug
  use preclude a White House future? Will Christian conservatives
  forgive Rudy Giuliani his two divorces? Will voters forgive
  Hillary Clinton for forgiving Bill?
  And what exactly did Democratic candidate Dennis Kucinich see
  hovering above actress Shirley MacLaine's house 25 years ago?
  This fall, Ms. MacLaine revealed in her new book that the Ohio
  congressman had seen a UFO and felt "a connection in his heart
  and heard directions in his mind." In a Democratic presidential
  debate in late October, Mr. Kucinich acknowledged seeing
  something airborne that he couldn't identify and then defused
  the issue with a joke about opening a campaign office in
  Roswell, N.M., the capital of unexplained sightings.
  Since then, the long-shot candidate has refused to elaborate on
  the experience.
  Now, after keeping quiet about the incident for a quarter of a
  century, the two people who say they were at Mr. Kucinich's side
  that evening have come forward to describe an event which they
  say left them convinced that there's intelligent life in outer
  space.
  "At no time did I feel afraid, even though I felt very small,"
  says one witness, Paul Costanzo. "I sensed that I was in the
  presence of a greater technology and intelligence."
  The close encounter, says Mr. Costanzo, took place in September
  1982 at Ms. MacLaine's former home in Graham, Wash. - an
  expansive estate on a ridge above the Puyallup River, with a
  view of Mount Rainier.
  The 61-year-old Mr. Kucinich, who declined several requests to
  comment for this article, had been the wunderkind mayor of
  Cleveland in the late 1970s and had met Ms. MacLaine through
  Bella Abzug, the late New York congresswoman and feminist. The


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m03-002.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:29]
Witnesses Describe Kucinich's Close Encounter

  actress says she quickly realized she and Mr. Kucinich were
  kindred spirits. Years later he asked Ms. MacLaine to be the
  godmother of his daughter.
  "We just thought the same," Ms. MacLaine says in an interview.
  "We have the same political points of view."
  When Cleveland voters ousted Mr. Kucinich after one tumultuous
  term, Ms. MacLaine offered him her home as a sanctuary where he
  could write his memoirs. He lived there for the better part of a
  year.
  Also in residence was Mr. Costanzo, a Juilliard-trained trumpet
  player and jujitsu black belt, who worked as Ms. MacLaine's
  assistant, personal trainer and bodyguard. He and Mr. Kucinich
  became good friends, and Mr. Costanzo, now 55 years old, served
  as deputy campaign director and security chief for the
  congressman's unsuccessful 2004 presidential run.
  Ms. MacLaine - well-known for her fascination with things
  mystical and extraterrestrial - was in Canada that weekend in
  1982, performing her one-woman show. But Mr. Costanzo's
  girlfriend at the time, a model and actress who is now 50 years
  old, was visiting when the UFO incident took place. She spoke
  after Mr. Costanzo requested she do so, and on condition that
  her name not be published.
  Here's what happened, according to separate interviews with Mr.
  Costanzo and his former girlfriend:
  The day was strange from the start. For hours, Mr. Kucinich, Mr.
  Costanzo and his companion noticed a high-pitched sound. "There
  was a sense that something extraordinary was happening all day,"
  says the girlfriend. She and Mr. Costanzo say that none of the
  three consumed alcohol or took drugs.
  As they sat down to a dinner, Mr. Kucinich spotted a light in
  the distance, to the left of Mount Rainier. Mr. Costanzo thought
  it was a helicopter.
  But Mr. Kucinich walked outside to the deck to look through the
  telescope that he had bought Ms. MacLaine as a house gift. After
  a few minutes, Mr. Kucinich summoned the other two: "Guys, come
  on out here and look at this."
  Mr. Costanzo and his girlfriend joined Mr. Kucinich, where they
  took turns peering through the telescope. What they saw in the
  far distance, according to both witnesses, was a hovering light,
  which soon divided into two, and then three.
  After a few minutes, the lights moved closer and it became
  apparent that they were actually three charcoal-gray, triangular
  craft, flying in a tight wedge. The girlfriend remembers each
  triangle having red and green lights running down the edges,
  with a laser-like red light at the tail. Mr. Costanzo recalls
  white lights, but no tail.
  Mr. Costanzo says each triangle was roughly the size of a large
  van, while his former girlfriend compares it to a "larger
  Cessna, smaller than a jet certainly." Neither recalls seeing
  any markings, landing gear, engines, windows or cockpits.
  The craft approached to within 200 yards, suspended over the
  field just beyond the swimming pool. Both witnesses say it
  emitted a quiet, throbbing sound - nothing like an airplane
  engine.
  "There was a feeling of wanting to communicate something, but I
  didn't know what," says Mr. Costanzo.
  The craft held steady in midair, for perhaps a minute, then sped
  away, Mr. Costanzo says. "Nothing had landed," he says. "No
  strange beings had disembarked. No obvious messages were beamed
  down. When they were completely out of sight, we all looked at
  each other disbelieving what we had seen."
  At Mr. Kucinich's suggestion, they jotted down their impressions
  and drew pictures to memorialize the event. Mr. Kucinich kept
  the notes, according to Ms. MacLaine, who said he promised her
  recently that he would try to find them.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m03-002.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:29]
Witnesses Describe Kucinich's Close Encounter

  "It was proof to me that we're obviously not alone," says the
  girlfriend.
  The next day, the group spotted what they thought to be military
  helicopters buzzing around the valley where they had made the
  sighting. And the high-pitched sound remained.
  Mr. Kucinich called Ms. MacLaine in Canada to tell her what had
  happened. "He said it was beautiful, serene, and it moved him,"
  says Ms. MacLaine, who is supporting Mr. Kucinich's candidacy.
  "He was not afraid of it, let's put it that way. Seeing
  something that close and sophisticated and gentle."
  Ms. MacLaine says she has seen UFOs from a distance in New
  Mexico and Peru, but never up close. She was envious. "I'm the
  one who reports them, but they never make close visitation. What
  am I doing wrong?"
  None of the three reported the incident to the authorities. And
  over the years that followed, they shared the story with very
  few people. "Unfortunately, people are ridiculed when they say
  they've had these kinds of experiences, which is why I never
  came forward with it," says the girlfriend.
  Ms. MacLaine says she called Mr. Kucinich before she included
  his UFO sighting in her book, "Sage-ing while Age-ing," a
  recounting of her spiritual and professional journeys. "I can
  handle it," she says he told her.
  More recently, Mr. Kucinich has dodged it. Approached by The
  Wall Street Journal for comment in December - moments after he
  voted for a House resolution praising Christmas and Christianity
  - Mr. Kucinich looked unblinkingly ahead: "I don't have any
  comment," he said.

  Hi Brad
  Rather than make an immensely long and inevitably repetitive


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m03-010.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:33]
Re: Penniston NP Conference & King

  reply by answering point by point inside your text I've tried to
  cover everything in this general answer.
  I agree that neither the "a good 2 miles" nor the probable
  "about 2 miles" (re "probable", see below) which appear in
  slightly different contexts in the B and C statements can be
  accurate reportage if the times and durations also given in the
  Buran, Chandler and Penniston statements are correct.
  There is a certain consistency and realism in the latter. An
  outbound walk duration of ~45-50min consistent with the start
  times given by all parties (after initial report at 0300) and
  with the turnaround time given by Buran (0354) is also
  consistent with the homebound walk duration given by Penniston
  (45 min). And these durations are consistent with a total out-
  and-back trip distance from the truck to Penniston's claimed
  landing site, through the forest, across the field to the region
  of the farmhouse and back to the truck, again via the landing
  site to discover the imprints as claimed. With allowances for
  hunting around, obstacles in the dark, and the close encounter
  as originally reported, that could reasonably be done on foot in
  about 90-95 mins.
  Personally, if I was in a position to fabricate statements given
  to Halt, and if wanted those statements to confirm a fictitious
  2-mile chase of a lighthouse, I would not have fabricated the
  time-constraints described in the previous paragraph, I would
  have inserted times that allowed sufficient duration for said 4-
  mile round trip to have occurred.
  (Ironically, the account which does allow time for a 2-hour
  lighthouse pursuit is Penniston's post-1997 notebook story
  giving an inconsistent start time of 12:20, although of course
  the date is wrong.)
  Nevertheless the 2 miles is definitely inconsistent.
  How to interpret it? Burroughs _seems_ to say (certainly
  implies) that the entire 2 miles he refers to lies beyond the E
  edge of the forest. Cabansag says that they went 2 miles "past
  our vehicle", i.e. that the entire outbound distance on foot was
  2 miles, including the whole distance through the forest (~1/2
  mile) from the point of abandoning the truck only "100 m from
  the [Woodbridge] gate".
  Yes, by interpreting "a good 2 miles" as 2.5 miles you can say
  that both men are, without saying so, specifically identifying
  the same "vantage point" out there in the countryside beyond
  Butley which it is physically impossible that they could have
  reached in the stated time. We then have an anomaly inviting a
  rather uneconomical explanation, i.e. that these figures were
  deliberately inserted to implicate a particular point (Burrow
  Hill) for the purpose of somehow discrediting Halt's Dec 28
  sighting as the Orford Ness lighthouse. I tend to think this is
  an unwelcome complexifying, unless there is no other possible
  interpretation of the "2 miles". I think there may be.
  Similarly, both statements _can_ be interpreted as meaning that
  the lighthouse was the continuously-visible object of pursuit
  during about 2 miles, inasmuch as the language allows this
  interpretation without categorically offering another. As you
  point out this is also physically impossible because of the
  topographical obstrcution of lines of sight. So once again if
  we limit ourselves to the choice between literal exactitude and
  a deliberate imposture, then we force ourselves to go for
  imposture. Once again, whilst agreeing that this is possible I
  stop short of concluding that it is necessary and "absolutely
  certain".
  To me this polarisation seems an artificial imposition for the
  sake of enforcing a logical clarity which is just not there. I'm
  content to work with a more fuzzy - and, I would contend, more
  realistic - representation.
  When Cabansag says
  ". . . we thought it had to be an aircraft accident. So did CSC
  as well. But we ran and walked a good 2 miles past our vehicle,
  until we got to a vantage point where we could determine that
  what we were seeing was only a beacon light off in the distance"



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m03-010.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:33]

  measuring off time and distance against recognisable landmarks
  on an OS map of the area? If that's my expectation then I'm
  going to find his 2 miles difficult to understand and I have a
  serious problem. But based on the rest of the statement that
  isn't my expectation. IMO it's too confused to bear the weight
  of very detailed deconstruction.
  "We stopped the Security Police vehicle about 100 meters from
  the gate. Due to the terrain we had to [go] on by foot."
  But it is nearly 4 times that distance even to get from the gate
  to the first road junction where according to Burroughs they
  took a right turn. They drove a little way then took a left onto
  a forestry track. They drove up this track into the trees until
  it became impassable, and then began walking.
  It was not until after the close encounter and after walking
  through to the far side of the forest that they picked up the
  flashing beacon, according to Burroughs.
  Yet long before they got near the forest, said Cabansag, they
  spent a significant time on foot, watching the lights (including
  the yellow "beacon light"). When they were still 100m from the
  trees he saw a light move. This was radioed in and they carried
  on, approaching the red and blue lights with "extreme caution".
  They were still 50-70m from the beginning of the trees when Sgt
  Chandler showed up. They carried on towards the lights. Then as
  soon as they got to the edge of the forest, he seems to say, the
  blue and red lights vanished, but the yellow flashing beacon was
  "still" visible.
  It isn't just the beacon light that is displaced here, it is the
  geography of the area.
  Is Cabansag's story deliberately engineered to make us believe
  the lighthouse was seen from the start? Since it is easy to
  verify that the lighthouse could not have been visible from
  where Cabansag says he was when he saw it, and easy to verify
  that it could have been visible from where Burroughs' radically
  different and yet supposedly-also-engineered account says he
  was, I conclude that the joint effect is of some pretty shoddy
  engineering. Another supposed plot that shoots itself in the
  foot with fatal internal inconsistency. I can't believe in it.
  It seems clear to me that C has mentally transposed events that
  happened off the rough forestry track, quite deep in the woods,
  back onto the access road near the Woodbridge back gate,
  probably because he was confused and anxious in unfamiliar
  surroundings. When he seems to be saying that the lighthouse
  beacon was seen from near the back gate before they even entered
  the trees we need to be very suspicious of his mental map.
  Therefore anomalies in his estimates of distance will not be too
  surprising.
  In addition to transposing events geographically Cabansag's
  account seems to telescope events in time. The narrative
  sequence is not well anchored to identifiable times and places,
  and the other witnesses today disagree with his memory (or lack
  of it) as to who was where and when. But reduced to basics:
  Cabansag went through the forest and saw some odd lights he
  couldn't identify. He also saw one light that he _could_
  identify from a final "vantage point" as a "beacon light off in
  the distance". The vantage point could well have been when
  emerging from the forest edge at the top of the open field.
  In details of location and time order Cabansag's account does
  contradict Burroughs, but I think it reads like a palimpseset of
  impressions recollected from the night in the forest a week
  earlier. His recent "very confused" memories - his own words -
   reinforce this (to the point where Bruni suggests "missing
  time"). There is no evidence that C really knew exactly where he
  was or for how long, and a nervous new boy (as he is depicted by
  all) who had little idea where he was in an unfamiliar dark
  forest would have been impressionable, and a week later may well
  have parroted "2 miles" from somewhere - without appreciating
  the problem.
  The fact that the total Dec 26 expedition could well be close to
  about 2 miles is one possible origin. But as you point out there


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m03-010.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:33]
Re: Penniston NP Conference & King

  is the coincidence that the Halt expedition, which had occurred
  in the interim and was no doubt discussed during the week, did
  go about 2 miles. This suggests another possible source of
  influence. Cabansag's recent memory clearly shows imagery from
  the Halt affair mixed in - a silvery light with red and blue
  lights spinning in it and shedding "flakes of metal", which "was
  not the lighthouse . . . I saw the lighthouse, this wasn't it,
  it was to the right of the lighthouse." (Bruni, p 193) It may be
  that his statement to Halt in 1981 was already incorporating
  some of what he had heard talked about in the previous week,
  thinking that Halt was retracing their steps - hence the 2 miles
  and the exaggerated scale of the Dec 26 expedition in his
  memory.
  It's possible. It isn't "absolutely certain" that it cannot be
  so.
  Burroughs' "about 2 miles" is not so easy to discount. There is
  a reasonable possibility that he could have exaggerated the
  length of the whole affair in his memory a week later, exposed
  to the same influences, and as I suggested there could be a
  degree of unconscious confabulation that leads to Burroughs and
  Cabansag cementing a similar exaggeration. It is certainly not a
  certainty that this can be ruled out, even though Burroughs'
  accounts, old and new, seem much better grounded and less
  ambiguous than Cabansag's.
  Another possibility that I haven't seen discussed is whether
  Burroughs' statement really does say "2 miles".
  Within a few lines of that phrase on the same page Burroughs
  twice uses the abbreviation "min" for "minute", as in "after a
  min or 2 we got up" and "it was only there for a min & it just
  streaked away". I wondered if what he really wrote was "we
  followed it for about 2 mins"?
  I'm not sure of the answer to that question, having compared
  enlargements of various words containing "n". There are examples
  where the "n" shows a similar shape, though not so exaggerated,
  as in instances of "into", "moving", "fense", "ground" and
  "comming". There are many other cases where the "n" is much more
  rounded (especially where it occurs at the start of a word). His
  "l" as in "field", "flashing", "lights" etc is often much more
  loopy than the supposed "l" in "miles", but there are very
  similar looking "l"s also. I think one would have to say that if
  it's an "n" it's atypical, but it could be. At least, it isn't
  absolutely certain that it's not an "n".
  It would be interesting to know if this issue has ever been
  raised directly with Burroughs. Does anyone know?
  Meantime, I not that two minutes at 2mph walking speed would be
  about 120 yards. Something of that order could fit with the
  distance into the field measured by Robert McLean at which the
  lighthouse ceases to be visible because of the horizon elevation
  (126m). Burroughs says they went on to a point where they "just
  crossed a creek" before being summoned back by Buran (0354).That
  would have to be (judging from the OS map) at least as far as
  the small stream down by the Boast house.
  A very strict literal reader might say "Ah, but if they 'could
  see it was coming from a lighthouse' after 2 minutes when they
  were only half way down the field, why would they have been down
  at the bottom of the field near the farmhouse, with the beacon
  no longer visible (at lease not directly), before turning back?"
  Perhaps because in reality situations don't necessarily resolve
  neatly all in a moment. You might, when coming out of the
  forest, be suspicious that you're looking at a lighthouse, and
  when half way into the field you (or one or more of you) might
  even be pretty sure that it's a lighthouse. When it disappears
  one of you might say, "I reckon that was definitely a
  lighthouse, let's pack it in," and another might say, "Well,
  maybe, but we've not been called off yet. What we saw in the
  woods was no lighthouse and it came out here somewhere. Let's
  just go on a bit to make sure." So you head off down to the
  valley. Nothing further happens, and at 0354 Buran, monitoring
  your progress by radio, says that's enough.
  BTW, in considering the duration of visibility of the lighthouse
  for various purposes (including follow-ability, as well as


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m03-010.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:33]
Re: Penniston NP Conference & King

  unusual optical effects) we ought to consider the visibility of
  the beam above the horizon, inclusing the effects of possible
  coastal haze, and the optical refractivity at near-zero degrees
  elevation that night.
  I don't know if the weather has been investigated in detail (?),
  but it was said to be still, clear and frozen at ground level,
  so a surface inversion due to radiative night-time cooling is
  possible in the early hours of the morning. Also in this sort of
  locale the possibility exists of warmer air from the sea
  advected over the cold surface air, and there are frontal and
  subsidence inversions that depend on the location of passing
  pressure fronts. Anyway, a super-refractive (inversion) layer on
   the verge of an optical trapping gradient (~11-12 degC/100m)
  refracts a raypath downward at the rate of about 33 arcsecs per
  km, which would "correct" for about 5 arcmin of negative
  elevation due to earth curvature over a distance of about 8.8 km
  from the forest edge to the lighthouse (or about 1/6 of the
  diameter of the moon). I'm not sure to what extent inversion -
   and a haze layer which is often associated with the inversion
  boundary - might be a factor in extending the limits of
  visibility of the lighthouse or, perhaps equally relevant, in
  altering its appearance (looming and/or colour separation) and
  delaying recognition of it as a lighthouse.
  (Note: This cannot be a factor in the early sighting of the red
  and blue lights in forrest. A miraged white light on the horizon
  might show vertical colour separation, but even if the optical
  pathway existed for a superior mirage of the lighthouse in this
  case, which it evidently didn't, the red would be separated to
  the bottom and blue, green or violet componenents would go to
  the top. This is the opposite of the pattern originally reported
  by Burroughs and Penniston: blue below and a red light on the
  top. True, Penniston did claim in 1983 [as James Archer;
  Randles, Street & Butler, p.251] that his object had a blue
  light on the top and red lights below; but I don't think we need
  to take that seriously.)
  Does there seem to be a disproportionate attention given to the
  lighthouse in the original statements? Possibly so. They
  expicitly distinguish the UFO from the lighthouse. Nevertheless,
  an impression of "protesting too much" might be partly what
  gives plausibility to the idea that they are special pleading.
  But the witnesses might well be motivated to place some emphasis
  on seeing the lighthouse because it had no doubt become the
  subject of speculation in the days following Halt's expedition.
  They would want to say that they had seen and identified it in
  order to show that they were clear in their minds about the
  distinction between it and their own UFO. This they did, even if
  in Cabansag's case especially the distinction, whilst explicit
  even there, is not drawn very coherently.

  Martin Shough

  on the right side are worth paying attention to.

  >>I think the mistake here is regarding 'intelligence' as the
  >>benchmark when 'tool-making' is the what sets humans apart from
  >>our fellow creatures. Tool-making is convergent. Once that niche

  >>will follow.
  >>I realize that convergence is a complicated concept, but it's a

  >G'day Ed.
  >Forgive me, but I find your argument a little confusing. If
  >'tool-making' is what 'sets us apart' from other animals, surely
  >it cannot also be convergent, as this requires precisely that we
  >are _not_ set apart by this ability, but share it with other
  >species.
  Hi James,
  Another convergent trait is the nose of anteaters. Dining
  exclusively on ants and termites will cause a distinctive nose.
  Relying exclusively on tool-making will create a generalized
  humanoid shape.
  Another species, such as a dinosaur, relying on toolmaking,
  should also develop a humanoid shape. That's my point.
  Toolmaking, our niche, separates humans from other mammals.
  Any other living organism relying on tool-making will
  also develop a humanoid appearance. I expect the same is true
  for other star systems that harbor life or planets in our own solar
  system that may have supported life in the past. Humans are not
  special and we should expect our histories to be recapitulated
  anywhere there is life.
  Intelligence is not a niche. All living things are as
  intelligent as they need to be to survive.

                                              Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science
  From: Michael Tarbell <mtarbell.nul>
  Date: Wed, 02 Jan 2008 15:24:21 -0700
  Archived: Thu, 03 Jan 2008 09:36:34 -0500
  Subject: Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

  >From: James Molesworth <jtmol1.nul>
  >To: ufoupdates.nul
  >Date: Tue, 01 Jan 2008 15:53:12 +1100
  >Subject: Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science
  <snip>
  >This allows a huge array of strange arguments to be made. Thus,
  >a theist could argue that, if the possibility of an omnipotent
  >god existing is less than zero, and it should be unless there is
  >something contradictory about the concept, then an omnipotent
  >god (or an infinite number of them) would necessarily exist.
  >Further, as it is omnipotent, this god would have the ability to
  >interact with all the universes, and therefore it is necessarily
  >the case that a god (God?) does exist in this universe!

  James,
  I presume you meant to say, "...if the possibility of an
  omnipotent god existing is greater than zero...", although the
  prospect of negative probabilities is intriguing.
  This argument goes way back, and some philosopher (can't place
  his name just now) actually employed it in an 'analytic proof' of
  the existence of God, bless his heart. However, not everyone
  found his reasoning particularly compelling.
  And of course, it does produce a contradiction, since the same
  argument can be used to _rule_out_ the existence of an
  omnipotent God, i.e., a single universe without one excludes
  them all. All in all, a fairly vacuous construct.
  By no means does this trivialize the many-worlds paradigm, nor
  the larger issue of the duality of Everything vs. Nothing. It
  seems clear that a universe in which less than Everything
  happens is effectively one with arbitrary, underivable constants
  that are somehow a 'built-in' feature of existence itself, i.e.,
  it is _not_ the case that "anything and everything goes".
  This would seem to be in conflict with - or at least does not
  form a duality with - our concept of Nothingness, which
  intuitively is devoid of any content, including arbitrary
  constants. Hence, if the universe is incomplete in the sense
  that not everything will happen, then clearly it did not spring
  from Nothingness.
  Now my head hurts. I leave to the metaphysicists on the List
  (and there are some capable ones) to clear this up, while I
  retreat to more mundane topics, such as UFOs. Haven't put much
  of a dent in that either.

  Mike

  From: Nick Pope <contact.nul>
  Date: Thu, 3 Jan 2008 13:00:28 -0000

  Subject: Re: Faux Disclosure In The Works?

  >From: Franklin Fields <fields.nul>
  >To: ufoupdates.nul
  >Date: Wed, 2 Jan 2008 10:22:56 -0500 (EST)
  >Subject: Re: Faux Disclosure In The Works?
  <snip>
  >It is obvious but worth stating that only the non-classified
  >information will be released. I would assume that the MOD would
  >follow similar procedures as the U.S. DOD.
  <snip>
  Once released, all information - whatever the original level of
  classification - is regarded as having been declassified.
  Accordingly, when released, the word "Unclassified" is stamped
  over the original level of classification. Here is an example of
  this (a .pdf file) from the MoD website:
  http://tinyurl.com/zrx58
  However, with highly classified documents (particularly recent
  ones) it's more likely that some of the material will be
  withheld, under the Exemptions to the Freedom of Information
  Act. Here are some examples:
  http://www.foi.gov.uk/guidance/exsumm/sec24.htm
  http://www.foi.gov.uk/guidance/exsumm/sec26.htm
  http://www.foi.gov.uk/guidance/exsumm/sec27.htm

  Could it be a bird? Sure. But - as I said to the reporter - one
  has to take a holistic approach, interviewing the witness,
  examining the camera, analyzing the imagery scientifically,
  checking to see if anything was tracked on radar, etc. Without
  this, all anyone can do (as I did) is offer an initial opinion
  as to whether or not an image looks interesting and merits
  further study. Inevitably, in a newspaper article of this sort,
  my lengthy interview was boiled down to a couple of soundbites.
  The real value of this sort of story is twofold. Firstly, it
  keeps the UFO phenomenon in the public eye (The Sun is the UK's
  best-selling national daily newspaper and this story has been
  picked up by other media outlets). Secondly, it helps 'smoke
  out' other photos and videos. Many people have such imagery but
  have never sent it to anyone, either because they fear disbelief
  or ridicule, or because they don't know who to send it to. Once
  a newspaper runs a story like this, it encourages such people to
  come forward. I've already been sent another interesting photo
  as a result of this story.

SETI@Home Ramps Up Data Analysis




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 4

                                              SETI@Home Ramps Up Data Analysis
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 04 Jan 2008 08:40:49 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 04 Jan 2008 08:40:49 -0500
  Subject: SETI@Home Ramps Up Data Analysis



  Source: Science Daily.Com - Herndon, Virginia, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/3bzosf
  Jan. 3, 2008

  SETI.nul Ramps Up To Analyze More Data In Search Of
  Extraterrestrial Intelligence
  ScienceDaily - The longest-running search for radio signals from
  alien civilizations is getting a burst of new data from an
  upgraded Arecibo telescope, which means the SETI.nul project
  needs more desktop computers to help crunch the data.
  Since SETI.nul launched eight years ago, the project based at
  the University of California, Berkeley's Space Sciences
  Laboratory has signed up more than 5 million interested
  volunteers and boasts the largest community of dedicated users
  of any Internet computing project: 170,000 devotees on 320,000
  computers.
  Yet, new and more sensitive receivers on the world's largest
  radio telescope in Arecibo, Puerto Rico, and better frequency
  coverage are generating 500 times more data for the project than
  before. The SETI.nul software has been upgraded to deal with
  this new data as the search for extraterrestrial intelligence
  (SETI) enters a new era and offers a new opportunity for those
  who want to help find other civilizations in the universe.
  "The next generation SETI.nul is 500 times more powerful then
  anything anyone has done before," said project chief scientist
  Dan Werthimer. "That means we are 500 times more likely to find
  ET than with the original SETI.nul"
  According to project scientist Eric Korpela, the new data
  amounts to 300 gigabytes per day, or 100 terabytes (100,000
  gigabytes) per year, about the amount of data stored in the U.S.
  Library of Congress. "That's why we need all the volunteers," he
  said. "Everyone has a chance to be part of the largest public
  participation science project in history."
  The 1,000-foot diameter Arecibo dish, which fills a valley in
  Puerto Rico, is part of the National Astronomy and Ionosphere
  Center operated by Cornell University with funds from the
  National Science Foundation. Since 1992, Werthimer and his team
  have piggybacked on radio astronomy observations at Arecibo to
  record signals from space and analyze them for patterns that
  could indicate they were transmitted by an intelligent
  civilization.
  When the team's incoming data overwhelmed its ability to analyze
  it, the scientists conceived a distributed computing project to
  harness many computers into one big supercomputer to do the
  analysis. Since SETI.nul was launched, other distributed
  computing projects have arisen, from folding.nul to predict the
  three-dimensional tangle of a protein to the newly-launched


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m04-002.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:43]
SETI@Home Ramps Up Data Analysis

  cosmology.nul to model possible universes. Most are now on a
  platform called BOINC (Berkeley Open Infrastructure for Network
  Computing), which was developed by SETI.nul's director David
  Anderson so that the various projects could share resources.
  "There are now 42 projects on BOINC, and, until now, there has
  been enough computing power to go around," Werthimer said.
  What triggered the new flow of data was the addition of seven
  new receivers at Arecibo, which now allow the telescope to
  record radio signals from seven regions of the sky
  simultaneously instead of just one. With greater sensitivity and
  the ability to detect the polarization of the radio signals,
  plus 40 times more frequency coverage, Arecibo is set to survey
  the sky for new radio sources.
  These improvements also prime the telescope for an improved
  search for intelligent signals from space.
  "The multiple receivers help us weed out interference better and
  make us less susceptible to thinking that things terrestrial are
  extraterrestrial," Werthimer said.
  Werthimer noted that, despite the fact that UC Berkeley has been
  analyzing radio signals from space since 1978 on various
  telescopes, no telltale signals from an intelligent civilization
  have yet been found.
  "Earthlings are just getting started looking at the frequencies
  in the sky; we're looking only at the cosmically brightest
  sources, hoping we are scanning the right radio channels," he
  said. "The good news is, we're entering an era when we will be
  able to scan billions of channels. Arecibo is now optimized for
  this kind of search, so if there are signals out there, we or
  our volunteers will find them."
  SETI.nul has been funded by various organizations over the
  years, including the Planetary Society and Sun Microsystems, and
  continues to be supported by individual donations from its
  volunteers.
  Adapted from materials provided by University of California -
  Berkeley.

                                                       WSJ's UFO Confuses E&P
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 04 Jan 2008 09:00:11 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 04 Jan 2008 09:00:11 -0500
  Subject: WSJ's UFO Confuses E&P



  Source: Billy Cox's Blog | De Void - Sarasota, Florida, USA
  http://www.heraldtribune.com/article/20080103/BLOG32/369621566
  Thursday, Jan. 3, 2008

  WSJ's UFO Confuses E&P
  By Billy Cox
  billy.cox.nul
  So the ink isn't even dry on The Wall Street Journal's 1A story
  Wednesday providing additional eyewitness details on Dennis
  Kucinich's 1982 UFO sighting when Editor & Publisher takes its
  first shot.
  Sensing a rogue and cheapening shift in the wind at the hands of
  new WSJ owner Rupert Murdoch, E&P asks: "Was there really any
  pressing need to cover Dennis Kucinch's old, and much laughed
  over, UFO encounter, especially with him about to poll about 1%
  of the vote in Iowa?"
  Hint to E&P: Compare the Web site traffic of your hand-wringing
  to the numbers recorded by reporter Michael M. Phillips's piece
  at:
  http://tinyurl.com/2t6w5j
  Here's the deal. Murdoch frequently displays the instincts of a
  dung beetle, but that's because he sometimes knows his audience
  better than J-school critics do.
  Phillips' reporting stands out not because he sensationalised
  it, but because the guy played it straight. The traditional
  formula for covering UFO stories like this is to place a phone
  call to the Committee for Skeptical Inquiry or some other expert
  who wasn't there to explain why Kucinich and others saw Venus or
  swamp gas instead. That's considered 'balance'.
  E&P is the watchdog of an industry in the throes of a horrific
  meltdown with no end in sight. The godawful details of its
  hastening irrelevance are most recently itemized at:
  http://tinyurl.com/2rnfvr
  That's where print analyst Alan Mutter describes how publicly
  traded newspaper companies have lost 42 percent of their market
  value, or $23 billion, since 2004.
  But it's the WSJ that draws arched eyebrows for trying to buck a
  trend. It decides to cover a UFO story the way it might also
  report a murder - by talking to witnesses and, without judgment,
  letting the facts speak for themselves.

  >What could cause the human eye to miss recognizing an object in

  The obvious answer is the human mind. We routinely 'edit out'
  peripheral data in the visual field in order to concentrate the
  mind's attention on what we believe ourselves to be actually
  'looking at' (looking is not a passive activity, and invariably
  involves some focus of attention to create an 'intended
  object'). In this case, by the photographer's reported
  admission, the intended object was a bay with two tankers
  forming an interesting view. In composing the shot, the
  photographer would quite naturally ignore the presence of a bird
  in the distance, and forget about its presence almost instantly.
  When looking at the photograph later, the photographer sees the
  object, not moving as it was at the time and therefore easy to
  identify and interpret at a subconscious level, frozen in flight
  - an artificial representation, and one that can appear
  deceptively mysterious.
  <snip>
  >- Mind control. Manipulation of the brain such that it does not
  >process or ignores data collected from the eyes in a controlled
  >fashion, while having no effect on the CCD imager, camera CPU
  >processor, or data storage. (I doubt it, but -hey- it's
  >possible).
  Yes, that's right, but not exercised by an external agency. It
  is the same self-administered mind control that babies start
  learning in the first few minutes after birth: the process of
  sorting out data in the visual field, interpreting it, and then
  making decisions about what parts of the data to focus
  concentration on, and what parts to set aside.
  This is one good, basic reason why photographs and films on
  which apparently anomalous data 'appears' ex post should always
  be subject to an extra dose of the most rigorous scrutiny.

  --
  Gerald O'Connell

Will A New Year Bring New Visitors?




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 4

                                               Will A New Year Bring New Visitors?
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 04 Jan 2008 09:14:46 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 04 Jan 2008 09:14:46 -0500
  Subject: Will A New Year Bring New Visitors?



  Source: The Tecumseh Countywide News - Oklahoma, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/39r4zx
  Thursday, January 03, 2008

  Will A New Year Bring New Visitors?
  By Lori Goat
  The recent sighting of an Unidentified Flying Object over a lake
  in Oklahoma City has put UFOs back on the public radar again.
  Pottawatomie County has had its share of strange lights in the
  sky.
  On New Year's Eve 2006 at 7:45 p.m., a retired Air Force
  operator and former AWACS crew member reported witnessing a
  bright light maneuvering unlike any known aircraft 2,000 feet
  above Tecumseh for about 40 seconds.
  Did aliens from another planet drop in to Tecumseh skies to help
  ring in a New Year?
  There are several other county connections to UFOs. Eyewitness
  reports of these peculiar lights in the sky are kept in the
  database of The National UFO Reporting Center (NUFORC).
  The center, founded in 1974 by a famous UFO investigator Robert
  J. Gribble, keeps tabs on nationwide UFO sightings. Law
  enforcement agencies, flight service stations, military
  facilities, 911 emergency dispatch centers, and organizations
  such the National Weather Service and NASA direct calls they
  receive about possible UFO's to the Center.
  According to NUFORC's files, there have been 404 unexplained
  sightings of UFOs in Oklahoma since 1947, six of them in Shawnee
  and Tecumseh.
  The most recent was on January 7, 2007, at 10:30 p.m., when a
  bright object with red lights flashed erratically across the
  Shawnee night for about a minute and a half.
  One of the most thoroughly documented sightings of UFOs in the
  county happened on May 10, 1998.
  The Oklahoma Highway Patrol (OHP) reported that patrolmen in
  three police cars cruising the Shawnee area saw diamond-shaped
  formations in the sky for 45 minutes that changed colors from
  red to white. Highway Patrol headquarters received so many calls
  on the lights that its teletype was jammed.
  OHP's official report stated the sightings came from Purcell
  north through Norman to Chandler and back through Meeker and
  Shawnee. It also stated, "Oklahoma Highway Patrol units 26, 30,
  and 40 have also made visual sightings. Tinker Air Force Base
  (TAFB) has had from 7 to 12 of them on radar, at this time, and
  they advise that they are flying at approximately 22,000 feet."


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m04-009.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:46]
Will A New Year Bring New Visitors?


  Although the sighting didn't happen in Pottawatomie County, an
  August 1965 UFO event in Oklahoma captured nationwide headlines.
  The OHP reported that TAFB had tracked four UFOs simultaneously
  and that they had descended very rapidly, from 22,000 feet to
  4,000 feet in seconds. Project Blue Book (one of a series of UFO
  studies conducted by the Air Force from 1952 to 1969) determined
  TAFB had mistaken Jupiter or the stars Rigel or Betelgeuse for
  UFOs.
  Robert Riser, director of the Oklahoma Science and Art
  Foundation Planetarium publicly rebuked Blue Book's findings.
  "This is as far from the truth as you can get. These stars and
  planets are on the opposite side of the earth from Oklahoma City
  at this time of year. The Air Force must have had its star
  finding chart upside down during August," he said.
  There is no doubt that unidentified flying objects exist and
  have been reported throughout history. Flying saucers have
  been depicted in ancient cave drawings.
  Are these objects from outer space or from an alien source? No
  one has a proven, definitive answer, but Gordon Cooper, the late
  astronaut from the county, had an "unshakable" belief of the
  validity of UFOs and extraterrestrials.
  Cooper was the pilot of the Mercury Faith 7 spacecraft and the
  Gemini 5 mission. Yet, it wasn't in space that he had his brush
  with aliens. It was at a military base in Germany and at Edwards
  Air Force Base in California.
  According to interviews with Cooper, while he was in Germany,
  unknown crafts were spotted over an air base. Thinking the
  objects could be Russian MIG-15s that regularly flew over the
  base, Sabre jets were scrambled to intercept.
  Upon closer inspection, Cooper said the crafts were metallic
  silver and saucer-shaped, flying above 45,000 feet, the maximum
  ceiling for any known jet at that time.
  While stationed at Edwards Air Force Base in 1957, Cooper had
  his second experience with a UFO. He was one of the test pilots
  in charge of the installation of a precision landing system. As
  his crew was filming the installation, they noticed a saucer fly
  overhead, hover, extend three legs as a landing gear, and land
  on a dry lakebed.
  As Cooper's camera crew got within 20 or 30 yards of the smooth,
  silver, about 30 foot in diameter saucer, it ascended and flew
  away.
  According to Cooper, the film of the saucer was developed and
  sent to Washington. It was never mentioned again, and when
  Cooper inquired about it at a later date, he was told it
  couldn't be found.
  Cooper believed so strongly in UFOs, he addressed a United
  Nations panel discussion on UFOs and ETs before his death.
  An excerpt from Cooper's speech:
  "I believe that these extraterrestrial vehicles and their crews
  are visiting this planet from other planets which obviously are
  a little more technically advanced than we are here on Earth. I
  feel that we need to have a top level, coordinated program to
  scientifically collect and analyze data from all over the earth
  concerning any type of encounter, and to determine how best to
  interface with these visitors in a friendly fashion."
  Cooper wasn't the only astronaut who believed in UFOs and ETs.
  Dr. Edgar Mitchell, Apollo 14 astronaut, has publicly stated
  that "We all know UFOs are real. All we need to ask is, where do
  they come from?"
  So look to the stars as this new year begins. Who knows what may
  come next?

'Hobbits' May Have Been Genetic Mutants




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 4

                                           'Hobbits' May Have Been Genetic Mutants
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 04 Jan 2008 09:19:12 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 04 Jan 2008 09:19:12 -0500
  Subject: 'Hobbits' May Have Been Genetic Mutants



  Source: National Geographic News - Washington DC, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/2rppaa
  January 3, 2008

  'Hobbits' May Have Been Genetic Mutants
  John Roach
  National Geographic News
  A rare disease characterized by small brain and body size but
  near normal intelligence is caused by mutations in a gene coding
  for the protein pericentrin, researchers have found.
  The scientists speculate that the condition may explain the
  tiny, hobbitlike people that occupied a remote, Indonesian
  island about 18,000 years ago=97adding fuel to the debate over
  whether the unusual creatures were a new species or just
  diseased modern humans.
  Pericentrin helps separate chromosomes during cell division,
  which is needed for growth.
  "The whole body loses its capacity to grow, because cell
  division is so difficult for people with this defect," said
  study co-author Anita Rauch of the Institute for Human Genetics
  at the University of Erlangen in Germany.
  On average, disease sufferers grow about three feet (a meter)
  tall and have a brain the size of a three-month-old baby.
  However, their intelligence is near normal.
  People with the defect also exhibit subtle bony anomalies in
  their hands and wrists, skull asymmetry, small chins, abnormal
  teeth, and abnormal shoulders, Rauch said.
  Mysterious Hobbit
  Descriptions of the hobbitlike people match those of modern
  humans with this genetic defect, Rauch added.
  When the hobbit was discovered in 2004 on the Indonesian island
  of Flores, scientists hailed it as a new species: Homo
  floresiensis.
  Since then, scientists have debated whether the hobbit is indeed
  a new species or a modern human with a genetic disease that
  causes small brains called microcephaly.
  The new study links the genetic mutations to a type of
  microcephaly that limits all growth=97that of the brain and the
  body.
  "We think it is very likely that Homo floresiensis indeed had a
  pericentrin mutation," Rauch said.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m04-010.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:47]
'Hobbits' May Have Been Genetic Mutants


  She added that, on islands like Flores, inherited diseases
  become commonplace because of the higher levels of mating among
  closely related people.
  The finding is reported online today in the journal Science.
  Down to the Details
  Richard Potts, director of the human origins program at the
  Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C., closely monitors
  the scientific debate over Homo floresiensis.
  He said the new study's link between genetics and human growth
  is "neat" but disagreed with the suggestion that Homo
  floresiensis represents a modern human with a genetic disorder.
  Proof that the hobbit is indeed a unique species, he said, is
  found in recent detailed studies of its wrist and upper arm
  bone.
  A wrist bone study published in Science last September found
  that the hobbit's wrist bones were primitive, like those in
  gorillas or chimpanzees.
  No known genetic diseases, including any type of microcephaly,
  results in an apelike wrist similar to the hobbit's, the authors
  of the wrist bone study concluded.
  "For many of us in the field, we have taken those studies,
  especially the one [on the wrist bone] as really being the death
  blow to the idea that we're dealing with a modern human," Potts
  said.
  And even if the researchers find a gene in the hobbits connected
  with dwarfism in modern humans, they would "still have to go
  down to the details of the morphology and try to explain
  [them]," he added.
  Dean Falk is an anthropologist at Florida State University in
  Tallahassee who has led several studies demonstrating Homo
  floresiensis is a unique species, not a diseased modern human.
  She commented via email that the new study is unconvincing=97for
  one, the pictures shown of people with this defect look nothing
  like the hobbit.
  "Their heads are too large relative to their bodies, the limb
  proportions are all wrong, the profiles of the face do not come
  close, and these individuals are from 8 to 12 years old," she
  wrote.
  The hobbit fossil, known as LB1, is from an individual about 30
  years old.
  Modern Variation
  Study co-author Rauch and her colleagues, meanwhile, hope that
  improved technology may soon allow them to extract DNA from the
  Flores fossils and test it for mutations to the pericentrin
  gene.
  The new research, Rauch noted, demonstrates that a single
  genetic defect can lead to miniaturization and distinct bone
  shape in humans.
  Rauch also plans to investigate connections between pericentrin
  mutations and natural variation in the modern human population.
  She said that there are a lot of small changes in the gene
  between normal people=97not enough to cause dwarfism but
  sufficient to make one person smaller than another, for example.
  "If you don't have the full mutation which leads to absence [of
  the protein]," she said, "but only a little change, this might
  cause little differences in the normal population."

  [Thanks to 'THe Norm' for the lead]

  From: David Rudiak <drudiak.nul>

  >From: Michael Tarbell <mtarbell.nul>
