  ><snip>
  >And of course, it does produce a contradiction, since the same
  >argument can be used to _rule_out_ the existence of an
  >omnipotent God, i.e., a single universe without one excludes
  >them all. All in all, a fairly vacuous construct.
  >By no means does this trivialize the many-worlds paradigm, nor
  >the larger issue of the duality of Everything vs. Nothing. It
  >seems clear that a universe in which less than Everything
  >happens is effectively one with arbitrary, underivable constants
  >that are somehow a 'built-in' feature of existence itself, i.e.,
  >it is _not_ the case that "anything and everything goes".
  While we're into speculation, it has also been proposed that
  with perhaps infinite possible universes, it may be that only
  some, by pure chance or constraints of some specific geometries,
  will produce any constants or the right combination of constants
  such that life, intelligence, and consciousness can arise at
  all.
  To take a simpleminded example, only in plane geometry will the
  interior angles of a triangle always add up to exactly 180
  degrees. In any of an infinite number of possible curved
  geometries, the total of the angles can take on an infinite
  number of possible values, therefore, no longer constant. For
  example, on the Earth's spherical surface, stand on the equator
  and shoot a line to the north pole for one leg of a triangle, go
  a quarter of the way around the equator to form another leg, and
  then shoot another line up to the pole for the third leg. All
  interior angles of the spherical triangle are 90 degrees in this
  case and add up to a total of 270 degrees. Had we gone halfway
  around the globe, however, the two angles at the equator would
  still have been 90 degrees each, whereas the apex of the
  triangle at the pole would have an angle of 180 degrees, and the
  total would be 360 degrees.
  Thus any sum of the angles of a triangle on a spherical geometry
  will always be greater than 180 degrees and will have no fixed
  value, as in plane geometry. So only plane, flat geometry, out
  of all the spatial geometries, creates an "arbitrary" constant
  of 180 degrees and imposes other constraints as to what can and
  cannot be in the formal system of deductive logic that arises
  from it.
  In the same sense, our universe may have some fundamental
  underlying mathematics that constrains what can and cannot be
  and forces our particular physical laws, which just happen to
  give rise to us. But other universes and underlying mathematics


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m04-014.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:49]
Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

  may have no such constraints (or different ones), and thus
  either have different physical laws that don't work to produce
  life or perhaps be undefinable and totally chaotic.
  This is a more cosmic version of Earth as a "Goldilocks planet,"
  i.e., a planet of just the right size with just the right type
  of parent star, in just the right orbit, etc., etc., to give
  rise to intelligent life. The same may be true of universes,
  with a few Goldilocks universes like our own amongst many
  clunkers. The odds of winning the lottery may be extremely
  small, but if enough lottery tickets are purchased, somebody
  eventually wins the lottery.
  In this theory, there is no intelligence that guides the
  formation of universes. Instead universes with definable
  physical laws and suitable physical constants that lead to life
  and intelligence happen through pure chance, that is, the
  lottery winners.
  >This would seem to be in conflict with - or at least does not
  >form a duality with - our concept of Nothingness, which
  >intuitively is devoid of any content, including arbitrary
  >constants. Hence, if the universe is incomplete in the sense
  >that not everything will happen, then clearly it did not
  >spring from Nothingness.
  In modern physics, the universe can arise from nothingness.
  Think of our existence as a giant bank loan. The money enables
  us to do and purchase all sorts of things, but on a ledger our
  net worth still adds up to zero because this is balanced by the
  debt owed back to the bank. Still one can live the high life as
  long as the loan isn't called back in. As some physicist like to
  say, the universe is the ultimate free lunch.
  The fundamental currency of the universe is energy and our
  existence is based on a positive energy "loan", balanced by a
  the negative energy owed back to the cosmic "bank" or "vacuum"
  or "zero state". In this metaphor, our loan gradually dwindles
  as useful energy disipates into the chaos we call entropy.
  Eventually, our universe will expand to such an extent and be so
  thin with matter that all physical interactions will essentially
  end, temperature will be down to absolute zero, nothing will
  move, and time, or change, will cease. This gloomy scenario is
  called the Big Chill. It makes me shudder and want to huddle by
  a fire just to think about it.
  >Now my head hurts. I leave to the metaphysicists on the List
  >(and there are some capable ones) to clear this up, while I
  >retreat to more mundane topics, such as UFOs. Haven't put much
  >of a dent in that either.
  Usually when philosophers heads begin to hurt from their own
  logical conclusions, they head down to the local pub for a pint
  or two or three. It's been known to help, at least until
  morning.

  David Rudiak

                                             Political Spotlight Brings UFO Group In
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Sat, 05 Jan 2008 20:24:25 -0500
  Archived: Sat, 05 Jan 2008 20:24:25 -0500
  Subject: Political Spotlight Brings UFO Group In



  Source: The Seattle Times - Washington, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/35y8d5
  Thursday, January 3, 2008

  Political Spotlight Brings UFO Group In From The Fringe
  By Jeffrey Weiss
  The Dallas Morning News

  Dallas =97 Anyone who takes the topic seriously knows about what
  they call the "giggle factor."
  So when Democratic presidential candidate Dennis Kucinich was
  asked in a recent debate about his belief in unidentified flying
  objects, the North Texas members of Mutual UFO Network (MUFON)
  weren't surprised when it turned into a political punch line.
  On the other hand, New Mexico Gov. Bill Richardson also has
  addressed UFOs =97 seriously =97 on the campaign trail. And in
  November, a group of highly credentialed aviation experts from
  around the world called for more official investigations of
  UFOs.
  Getting their cause into the news =97 and not just as a joke =97 is
  welcome to people who have felt pushed to the fringes for a long
  time.
  "There is a growing awareness and willingness on the part of the
  public to take this seriously," said Ken Cherry, the Texas MUFON
  director.
  Is the secret that the ufologists of MUFON have been chasing for
  decades about to come out?
  "We don't think it's a secret. Just some people don't believe
  it," said Terry Groff, Web master for the local MUFON group and
  a trained UFO investigator.
  He was one of about two dozen members who assembled for a
  regular meeting last month at an Irving, Texas, public library.
  Organizers say they've filled a hall with more than 100 people
  for meetings where a particularly popular speaker appears.
  Outsiders often misunderstand the purpose of the organization,
  Cherry said.
  "People want us to confirm their claims," he said. "That is not
  our job."
  Most UFO sightings quickly become IFOs after a little
  investigation, he said. Airplanes, satellites, model rockets,
  helicopters =97 all of these can fool an untrained eye. But all of
  those valid explanations still leave a few unexplainables.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m05-001.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:49]
Political Spotlight Brings UFO Group In


  Those few are what the ufologists say make them think there's
  more to know =97 but they aren't necessarily sure what the "more"
  is.
  "I really haven't made my mind up," said MUFON regional director
  James Shatley. "The preponderance of evidence is that either we
  have discovered incredible technology, or there are some other
  races that have conquered time and space and figured out how to
  get here."
  For all the scientific aspirations of MUFON, it's a mash-up of a
  serious amateur investigation club and a support group for
  people who say there is Something =97 or Someone =97 Out There.
  "We have had people come to our meetings who literally wear a
  protective hat to protect themselves from aliens invading their
  thoughts," Cherry said.
  The members of his group try to be welcoming and not dismissive
  of them, he said. After all, they all know what it's like to be
  ridiculed for their ideas.
  "I don't think we've ever had a bad experience where someone
  that everyone thought was off-the-wall came and they didn't go
  away feeling good," Cherry said.
  On this afternoon, nobody was wearing an odd hat. After a bit of
  business, they settled in to watch a decade-old video of a
  speech made at a previous meeting. The speaker was Jim Marrs,
  the Texan author of "Crossfire" =97 a book Oliver Stone drew on
  for the conspiracy-filled plot of his movie "JFK" =97 and "Alien
  Agenda," Marrs' account of government suppression of information
  about UFOs.
  It's safe to say Marrs' views about UFOs are as accepted by most
  scientists as his ideas about the Kennedy assassination are by
  most historians. But this was his home crowd, and they listened
  attentively as he recounted tales of the supposed UFO crash at
  Roswell, N.M., the odd crop circles and other stories ufologists
  say have never been explained.
  After the video, Marrs 'appeared' live via a cellphone held up
  to a microphone and took questions.
  "There may be more breathtaking discoveries coming out in the
  coming months," he said.
  The recent mainstream news about UFOs did not seem likely to
  produce a revelation any time soon.
  Kucinich said he saw a UFO 25 years ago while visiting Shirley
  MacLaine's home in Washington state. Richardson pledged to
  reopen the famous case of aliens reportedly crashing at Roswell
  in 1947.
  The aviation experts calling for more investigation included a
  deputy chief of staff from the Belgian air force, the retired
  chief of Accidents and Investigations for the Federal Aviation
  Administration, a pilot with the Chilean Aviation Army, an Air
  France captain, a general in the Iranian air force and a
  representative from the United Kingdom's Ministry of Defense.
  The group spoke in support of a petition that said, in part: "We
  maintain that a restive, concerned public has the right to be
  informed of the facts about UFO incidents that are well-
  documented and involve multiple witnesses."
  Not all the MUFON members claim to have seen UFOs. But some do
  have their stories.
  Lucy Jane Mock, whose husband was in the Air Force, believes she
  has seen several unexplainable things in the sky.
  "I hope you get to see one," she told a visitor to the meeting.
  "Thrilling!"

                                                          'Definitely Unidentified'
   From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
   Date: Sat, 05 Jan 2008 20:34:05 -0500
   Archived: Sat, 05 Jan 2008 20:34:05 -0500
   Subject: 'Definitely Unidentified'



   Source: The Ottawa Citizen - Ontario, Canada
   http://tinyurl.com/2o254u
   Friday, January 04, 2008
   [Frame-grab at site]

   'Definitely Unidentified'
   P.E.I. couple capture on videotape mystery object hurtling
   toward earth
   Charles Mandel
   The Ottawa Citizen

   A video of what appears to be an object trailing a dark
   spiralling plume behind it and plummeting toward Prince Edward
   Island's Northumberland Strait is the focus of intense
   speculation.
   A P.E.I. couple captured the strange event on video on Dec. 26,
   but witnesses and experts alike aren't certain what they're
   observing.
   "We were kind of dumbfounded," said Tony Quigley, the P.E.I.
   farmer who videotaped the apparent unidentified flying object
   with his wife, Marie Ford-Quigley.
   The couple was out walking late in the afternoon near North
   Tryon on the island's west end when Mr. Quigley spotted the
   mysterious object. "I said to Marie, 'Look, there's a plane in
   trouble there.' It looked like smoke coming from it."
   The couple taped the strange scene for nearly six minutes. Mr.
   Quigley estimates the object they saw was more than three
   kilometres high and is convinced that the UFO must have crashed
   in the strait or in New Brunswick.
   They watched the spectacle for close to 30 minutes and received
   calls from neighbours who also witnessed it.
   "I really didn't want to be looking forward to hearing that
   there was a plane crashing around the area and people losing
   their lives on Boxing Day," Mr. Quigley said.
   But calls the next day to the area's airport, Summerside RCMP
   and the federal Transportation Safety Board came up with no
   reports of plane crashes.
   Ms. Ford-Quigley speculates it might have been a fighter jet
   dumping fuel and in trouble. One thing's for sure: her husband
   isn't buying any stories about crashing flying saucers.
   "This is definitely unidentified," Mr. Quigley said. "But if


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m05-004.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:51]
'Definitely Unidentified'

   you're talking Martians or anything like that, I haven't seen
   any to date, so I can't say I really believe in them."
   That's not the case with Gertrude Campbell. The Quigleys'
   neighbour also saw the UFO, along with four other people. Ms.
   Campbell, 65, firmly believes in UFOs.
   "I swear when I come (home) at night time and I look at some of
   those stars and they're pretty big, I'd say that's what's
   looking over us," she said. But if the P.E.I. object was a
   saucer, then according to Ms. Campbell: "It broke up coming
   down."
   Don Ledger, a UFO researcher and author who lives in
   Bridgewater, N.S., believes the object was space junk. He cites
   the launch in mid-December of a NASA Atlas rocket carrying a
   satellite for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office, the
   agency that co-ordinates spy satellites south of the border.
   "Supposedly the booster came down around southwestern Nova
   Scotia," said Mr. Ledger, who co-wrote with Chris Styles, Dark
   Object, a book about a purported UFO crash at Shag Harbour,
   N.S., in 1967.
   "That (NASA booster) didn't make orbit the way it was supposed
   to, but I can't prove it.
   "After a certain point in its launch, everything goes what they
   call dark at NASA and it turns over to the spooks down there in
   the U.S. who handle the satellites. So if indeed it did come
   down, you're not going to hear about it."
   The Quigleys are sending their video to Ufology Research of
   Manitoba in Winnipeg, in hopes that the private, non-profit
   group can help solve the mystery.

  >>And of course, it does produce a contradiction, since the same
  >>argument can be used to _rule_out_ the existence of an
  >>omnipotent God, i.e., a single universe without one excludes
  >>them all. All in all, a fairly vacuous construct.
  >>By no means does this trivialize the many-worlds paradigm, nor
  >>the larger issue of the duality of Everything vs. Nothing. It
  >>seems clear that a universe in which less than Everything
  >>happens is effectively one with arbitrary, underivable constants
  >>that are somehow a 'built-in' feature of existence itself, i.e.,
  >>it is _not_ the case that "anything and everything goes".
  >While we're into speculation, it has also been proposed that
  >with perhaps infinite possible universes, it may be that only
  >some, by pure chance or constraints of some specific geometries,
  >will produce any constants or the right combination of constants
  >such that life, intelligence, and consciousness can arise at
  >all.
  >To take a simpleminded example, only in plane geometry will the
  >interior angles of a triangle always add up to exactly 180
  >degrees. In any of an infinite number of possible curved
  >geometries, the total of the angles can take on an infinite
  >number of possible values, therefore, no longer constant. For
  >example, on the Earth's spherical surface, stand on the equator
  >and shoot a line to the north pole for one leg of a triangle, go
  >a quarter of the way around the equator to form another leg, and
  >then shoot another line up to the pole for the third leg. All
  >interior angles of the spherical triangle are 90 degrees in this
  >case and add up to a total of 270 degrees. Had we gone halfway
  >around the globe, however, the two angles at the equator would
  >still have been 90 degrees each, whereas the apex of the
  >triangle at the pole would have an angle of 180 degrees, and the
  >total would be 360 degrees.
  >Thus any sum of the angles of a triangle on a spherical geometry
  >will always be greater than 180 degrees and will have no fixed
  >value, as in plane geometry. So only plane, flat geometry, out
  >of all the spatial geometries, creates an "arbitrary" constant
  >of 180 degrees and imposes other constraints as to what can and
  >cannot be in the formal system of deductive logic that arises
  >from it.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m05-009.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:53]
Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science


  >In the same sense, our universe may have some fundamental
  >underlying mathematics that constrains what can and cannot be
  >and forces our particular physical laws, which just happen to
  >give rise to us. But other universes and underlying mathematics
  >may have no such constraints (or different ones), and thus
  >either have different physical laws that don't work to produce
  >life or perhaps be undefinable and totally chaotic.
  >This is a more cosmic version of Earth as a "Goldilocks planet,"
  >i.e., a planet of just the right size with just the right type
  >of parent star, in just the right orbit, etc., etc., to give
  >rise to intelligent life. The same may be true of universes,
  >with a few Goldilocks universes like our own amongst many
  >clunkers. The odds of winning the lottery may be extremely
  >small, but if enough lottery tickets are purchased, somebody
  >eventually wins the lottery.
  >In this theory, there is no intelligence that guides the
  >formation of universes. Instead universes with definable
  >physical laws and suitable physical constants that lead to life
  >and intelligence happen through pure chance, that is, the

  >>This would seem to be in conflict with - or at least does not

  >In modern physics, the universe can arise from nothingness.
  >Think of our existence as a giant bank loan. The money enables
  >us to do and purchase all sorts of things, but on a ledger our
  >net worth still adds up to zero because this is balanced by the
  >debt owed back to the bank. Still one can live the high life as
  >long as the loan isn't called back in. As some physicist like to
  >say, the universe is the ultimate free lunch.
  >The fundamental currency of the universe is energy and our
  >existence is based on a positive energy "loan", balanced by a
  >the negative energy owed back to the cosmic "bank" or "vacuum"
  >or "zero state". In this metaphor, our loan gradually dwindles
  >as useful energy disipates into the chaos we call entropy.
  >Eventually, our universe will expand to such an extent and be so
  >thin with matter that all physical interactions will essentially
  >end, temperature will be down to absolute zero, nothing will
  >move, and time, or change, will cease. This gloomy scenario is
  >called the Big Chill. It makes me shudder and want to huddle by
  >a fire just to think about it.
  >>Now my head hurts. I leave to the metaphysicists on the List
  >>(and there are some capable ones) to clear this up, while I
  >>retreat to more mundane topics, such as UFOs. Haven't put much
  >>of a dent in that either.
  >Usually when philosophers heads begin to hurt from their own
  >logical conclusions, they head down to the local pub for a pint
  >or two or three. It's been known to help, at least until
  >morning.
  Apologies for not doing any snipping to shorten this, but the
  way it has been written means that it is not at all snip-
  friendly. Anyway, all of David's points are well-taken, but
  there are a few points I would like to add.
  The mathematics of zero and infinity are comparatively
  neglected. One consequence of this is that we don't really have
  a properly worked up conceptual framework for dealing with ideas
  that hinge upon them. When the 'infinite worlds' argument is put
  forward, the leap to 'all things must be possible and will
  therefore happen somewhere and somewhen' is a rather trite one.
  The argument still assumes a causal framework that is related to
  the one with which we are familiar, and it is not all clear that
  this justifies the 'all possibilities' inference. Picture, if
  you will, the world in which there are no laws of physics.
  Alternatively, picture the world in which all the different laws
  of physics from all the other worlds apply all of the time. And
  then another that includes all the physical laws from that last
  one, and so on. Compose examples of your own. You will soon
  start to see that 'infinity' is treacherous logical bedfellow


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m05-009.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:53]
Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

  and cannot be treated (thought about, conceptualised) in same
  way as, say, 'an unimaginably large number'.
  Zero, in the form of the 'nothingness' from which existence
  arises in the example to which David refers, is a similarly
  treacherous tool. In its purest form, it erases everything.
  Existence can then only be conceptualised as series of holes in
  nothing - a somehow more concentrated form of nothingness.
  Contemplating this state of affairs is a vertiginous experience
  to say the least, and one soon has a sense of the hopeless
  inadequacy of the conceptual framework that we have for
  undertaking such exercises.
  Finally, I must counsel a severe mistrust of all cosmological
  speculation that places 'intelligence' or 'consciousness' in any
  sort of privileged category. This is really nothing more than an
  absurd anthropocentric conceit. When encountering this sort of
  thing, stop to ask a few pointed questions: What evidence do we
  have to the effect that consciousness/intelligence is not just
  one more manifestation of complexity, and one that evolving
  monkeys (like us) pass through on the way to other, more complex
  and sophisticated, states? If that is so, why should we expect
  consciousness/intelligence to play any special role in the grand
  cosmological scheme? If we can't think beyond
  consciousness/intelligence in order to envisage a category of
  activity depending on a higher state of complexity, what does
  that tell us about the limitations of the
  consciousness/intelligence that we are so ready to congratulate
  ourselves for having attained?
  As above, compose your own examples. Once you get into the swing
  of it they come thick and fast. And all of them chip away quite
  devastatingly at that anthropocentric conceit that I so
  distrust.
  That's all. Right now, on the Rudiak/Tarbell scale of
  philosophical
  migraine, I find myself rapidly approaching the four pint mark...
  --
  Gerald O'Connell

  Yes, but even the most sophisticated camera will produce

  think that Maynard was referring to a phenomenon called Focal

  once caused by purely mechanical means-because of the way that
  the information is gathered from the imaging element.
  I think it's likely that the photo captured a bird, btw.

Truth Is Out As UK X-Files Go Public




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 6

                                              Truth Is Out As UK X-Files Go Public
  From: Joe McGonagle <joe.mcgonagle.nul>
  Date: Sun, 06 Jan 2008 01:30:44 +0000
  Archived: Sun, 06 Jan 2008 09:51:13 -0500
  Subject: Truth Is Out As UK X-Files Go Public

  Source: The Observer - London, UK
  http://tinyurl.com/ywr3pb
  Sunday January 6, 2008
  Mark Townsend
  Defence Correspondent

  The Truth Is Out: X-Files Go Public
  British UFO 'sightings' investigated by a secret branch of the
  MoD are soon to be revealed and officials are braced for a
  torrent of inquiries
  Without warning, the orange UFO swooped toward them. The crew of
  the RAF Vulcan bomber banked hard and radioed they were being
  chased across the Atlantic by a large mysterious object. The
  incident was classified as a UFO sighting and the details were
  immediately locked away.
  Now, 30 years later, the extraordinary encounter is among
  thousands of previously secret cases contained in the
  government's 'X-Files' that officials are to release in their
  entirety.
  The cases, many from a little-known defence intelligence branch
  tasked with investigating UFO claims, will be published by the
  Ministry of Defence to counter what officials say is 'the maze
  of rumour and frequently ill-informed speculation' surrounding
  Whitehall and its alleged involvement with Unidentifed Flying
  Objects.
  The public opening of the MoD archive will expose the once
  highly classified work of the intelligence branch DI55, whose
  mission was to investigate UFO reports and whose existence was
  denied by the government until recently. Reports into about
  7,000 UFO sightings investigated by defence officials - every
  single claim lodged over the past 30 years - are included in the
  files, whose staged release will begin in spring.
  The decision to release Whitehall's full back-catalogue of UFO
  investigations was taken last month after the Directorate of Air
  Space Policy, the government agency responsible for filtering
  sensitive reports, gave its permission to publish the biggest
  single release of documents in MoD history. Now the government
  fears a repeat of the unprecedented demand and the website crash
  experienced by the French national space agency in March when it
  released its own UFO files. Government IT experts are believed
  to have drawn up contingency plans to avoid a repeat scenario
  when Britain's dossiers are finally made public.
  Among the first tranche of UK cases will be the official
  government files into the famous Rendlesham incident, dubbed
  'Britain's Roswell' after the US incident when a flying saucer
  is said to have crash-landed in the New Mexico desert 60 years
  ago. On a foggy night in 1980 several witnesses reported a UFO
  apparently landing in Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk. Statements
  claimed the craft was covered in markings similar to Egyptian


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m06-001.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:58]
Truth Is Out As UK X-Files Go Public

  hieroglyphics and aliens emerged from it. Although a man later
  confessed to having staged the incident as a hoax, the files
  will clear up continuing speculation as to whether radiation was
  detected at the site after the event.
  Another case reported to the intelligence branch DI55 -
   Britain's version of the 'Men In Black' - chronicles a series
  of reports sent to RAF Scampton, Lincolnshire, by the crew of a
  Vulcan bomber on exercise over the Bay of Biscay early on 26 May
  1977. According to documents seen by The Observer, five crewmen,
  including the captain, co-pilot and navigators, watched 'an
  object' approach their aircraft at 43,000ft above the Atlantic.
  The mysterious craft then appeared to turn and follow their
  precise course from a distance of four miles.
  Initially, the crew said the object resembled landing lights
  'with a long pencil beam of light ahead' but as it turned
  towards them the lights suddenly went out leaving a diffuse
  orange glow with a bright fluorescent green spot in its bottom
  right-hand corner. Then, according to signals sent back to
  Scampton, the crew noted a mystery object 'leaving from the
  middle of the glow on a westerly track... climbing at very high
  speed at an angle of 45 degrees'.
  The Vulcan's navigator recorded interference on his radar screen
  from the direction of the UFO which continued for 45 minutes as
  the plane headed back to Britain. On return to the UK, the
  camera film from the aircraft's radar was examined by RAF
  intelligence. They found a 'strong response' from the direction
  of the sighting. The UFO was captured as 'an elongated shadow'
  of a 'large-sized' object travelling at a similar height to the
  Vulcan. An intelligence report sent to the MoD the same day says
  the crew 'were unable to offer a logical explanation for the
  sighting'.
  Although hailed as the complete disclosure of the UK's UFO
  files, questions are likely to remain over whether all available
  information will be made public. Despite the Vulcan sighting
  being investigated by DI55, no details remain in the file
  indicating what they found or what became of the radar film.
  The disclosures are more likely, claim some experts, to lend
  credence to the theory that such UFO incidents were, rather than
  alien visitations, military activities such as missile launches,
  testing of prototype aircraft and other activities during the
  Cold War.
  David Clarke, a lecturer in journalism at Sheffield Hallam
  University and author of Flying Saucerers: A Social History of
  UFOlogy, said: 'Something was definitely going on, but really
  these files show that the government did not know either. This
  release will be a source of disappointment or vindication for
  some, and embarrassment for others.
  'Conspiracy theorists who believe that the various governments
  of the world are hiding secrets about the "reality" of aliens
  will see this as another whitewash effort by the MoD and will
  probably continue their self-sustaining "campaign for the
  truth", when the truth will in fact now be "out there".'
  UFO researcher Joe McGonagle said: 'There will always be a hard
  core who believe these files were prepared for release and that
  there is a secret department within the military who has a
  separate stash of files that have not been disclosed.'
  UFOs remain one of the most popular subjects for Freedom of
  Information requests and the release is certain to generate a
  massive response from the public when the files are placed in
  the National Archives. Clarke, who has lodged hundreds of FoI
  requests, recently discovered that the government was
  considering destroying the 24 files created by DI55 because they
  were contaminated by asbestos. Not only were the UFO records
  polluted, but a total of 63,000 files estimated at between six
  to 12 million pages - most of them classified as secret - were
  facing the same fate. Having admitted the existence of the
  problem to Clarke, the MoD opted to instigate a =A33m project
  digitally to scan the files before they were destroyed. Scanning
  of the 24 contaminated UFO files owned by DI55 was completed
  last year, although it is understood that names of officials in
  the reports will be removed.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m06-001.shtml[09/12/2011 23:50:58]
Truth Is Out As UK X-Files Go Public

  Although the government remains reticent to discuss its
  intelligence work on UFOs, it is known that DI55 has been hot on
  the trail of flying saucers since the Sixties. Experts admit
  that they work closely with the security services MI5, MI6 and
  GCHQ to collect and assess evidence of potential threats to
  Britain.
  The decision by the UK to open its files could lead to the US
  government following suit. A group of former pilots and
  government officials recently urged the Pentagon to reopen
  investigations into claims of UFO sightings.
  UFO claims
  1980 Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk. US servicemen claim to have
  seen an alien craft and its landing site.
  1984 Minsk, USSR. Aeroflot pilots say they are pursued by a
  glowing shape.
  1989 Bonnybridge, Scotland. Fire crew report objects rushing
  towards them before veering away at the last moment.
  1990 Brussels, Belgium. Two F-16 fighter pilots recount being
  engaged in 75-minute mid-air chase with a UFO.

Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

                                              Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science
  From: Martin Shough <parcellular.nul>
  Date: Sun, 6 Jan 2008 16:26:16 -0000
  Archived: Sun, 06 Jan 2008 13:47:14 -0500
  Subject: Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

  >From: Gerald O'Connell <gac.nul>
  >Date: Fri, 4 Jan 2008 20:31:32 +0000
  >To: ufoupdates.nul
  >Subject: Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science
  >>From: David Rudiak <drudiak.nul>
  >>To: <ufoupdates.nul>
  >>Date: Thu, 3 Jan 2008 15:18:14 -0800
  >>Subject: Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science
  <snip>
  >>The fundamental currency of the universe is energy and our
  >>existence is based on a positive energy "loan", balanced by a
  >>the negative energy owed back to the cosmic "bank" or "vacuum"
  >>or "zero state".
  <snip>
  >Zero, in the form of the 'nothingness' from which existence
  >arises in the example to which David refers, is a similarly
  >treacherous tool. In its purest form, it erases everything.
  >Existence can then only be conceptualised as series of holes in
  >nothing - a somehow more concentrated form of nothingness.
  >Contemplating this state of affairs is a vertiginous experience
  >to say the least, and one soon has a sense of the hopeless
  >inadequacy of the conceptual framework that we have for
  >undertaking such exercises.
  I don't think this is quite right (although I sympathise with
  the sentiment). The quantum zero point is not 'nothingness...
  that erases everything', and this is just why states are said to
  be able to arise out of it.
  Nothingness as commonly conceived is a state which is
  functionally the same as an infinitesimal, and thus in some
  sense the reciprocal of infinity. But the zero point of energy
  in physics is rather better defined than nothingness. It is an
  average or expectation value of a system which, as David
  indicated, oscillates between positive and negative energy
  states. Classical zero is a unique true vacuum state where
  states of negative energy can have no meaning. Quantum zero is,
  in general, a _false-vacuum_ state that can have different
  values, and positive quantities can indeed be thought of as
  "holes in nothing" because nothing is redefined as a rational
  state.
  Infinity and infinitesimals have the problem of leading to
  catastrophe when introduced into calculations about real states,
  but fortunately, despite the famous "unreasonable effectiveness"
  of maths in producing entities that represent actuality, there
  doesn't seem to be any clear physical basis for these ideas. In
  classical physics any finite quantity at all can be infinitely
  differentiated, but in electromagnetic theory this leads to the
  ultraviolet catastrophe (equipartition of energy modes in cavity
  radiation) and has to be replaced by a quantum principle, as is
  well known. But what isn't quite so well known is that once
  introduced here the quantum principle is forced to run through
  the whole of physics to its spacetime foundations. If the energy


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m06-007.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:01]
Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

  of spacetime is classically differentiable than quantum theory
  fails for all other forces, because all other forces interact
  through gravity. This is at the heart of why the search for
  quantum gravity (QG) is such a big deal.
  But many discussions of quantum spacetime proceed as though
  there is a real differentiable continuum background underneath
  the quantisation. This has been one of the major problems of
  string theories for many years. The true QG theory will be
  radically quantised, and the notion of initesimal scale
  (infinitesimal gravitational potentials) will not appear in it.
  I tend to think that infinite scales (infinite gravitational
  potentials) must also be unphysical, and that therefore all
  possible physical states inside the universe will be
  representable as finite relations amongst a finite number of
  discrete elements. This would mean that there is a finite number
  of configurations of these elements, a finite number of
  discriminable universe-states, and thus a finite probability of
  occurrence of any given state (though not necessarily a finite
  probability of _re_currence). Logical paradoxes involving
  infinite numbers of antithetical states all having probabilities
  of 1.0 ought to be unphysical in a radically quantised cosmos,
  and that seems desirable.
  However the irony is that long after Planck and the subjugation
  of the troublesome infinities in the original QED theory, the
  whole question of infinity sneaks in again through an
  unsecurely-locked backdoor of the same quantum theory, which is
  the "measurement problem". Popular Everett-style approaches to
  "solving" the measurement problem, by proliferating an infinite
  number of "observers" collapsing wavefunctions in an infinite
  number of orthogonal worlds each with its own identical
  measurement problem, have brought in an "ultraviolet
  catastrophe" infinitely larger (in the Cantorian set-of-sets
  sense) than the classical infinite-energy catastrophe that QED
  was invented to cure in the first place!
  The huge irony of this seems often to be lost on us. The only
  "improvement" is that a number equal to infinity-minus-one of
  these other worlds is to be forever unobservable. Planck may as
  well have "solved" the cavity radiation problem in 1900 by
  saying that there really is infinite energy inside the cavity,
  but it must have gone into other dimensions. Thus he could have
  "saved the phenomena" for classical physics without needing to
  go to the trouble of founding quantum theory at all.
  If we accept that we are observing only one instance of a
  transfinite set of universes representing all possible states of
  all possible physical systems obeying all possible variations of
  all possible physical laws, then we can have infinity back - if
  we want it. I'm not convinced that we do, and prefer to think
  that there may be a more economical (and less anthropocentric)
  solution of the measurement problem than infinite numbers of
  "observers". When this is finally worked out I like to think
  that the vaccum will be differently understood yet again, and
  that taming it will involve an understanding of QG that
  radically changes how we think not only about spacetime but
  about quantum theory itself, and even the meaning and origin of
  what we call probabilities.

  Martin Shough

  >>>or "zero state".
  ><snip>
  >>Zero, in the form of the 'nothingness' from which existence
  >>arises in the example to which David refers, is a similarly
  >>treacherous tool. In its purest form, it erases everything.
  >>Existence can then only be conceptualised as series of holes in
  >>nothing - a somehow more concentrated form of nothingness.
  >>Contemplating this state of affairs is a vertiginous experience
  >>to say the least, and one soon has a sense of the hopeless
  >>inadequacy of the conceptual framework that we have for
  >>undertaking such exercises.
  >I don't think this is quite right (although I sympathise with
  >the sentiment). The quantum zero point is not 'nothingness...
  >that erases everything', and this is just why states are said to
  >be able to arise out of it.
  >Nothingness as commonly conceived is a state which is
  >functionally the same as an infinitesimal, and thus in some
  >sense the reciprocal of infinity. But the zero point of energy
  >in physics is rather better defined than nothingness. It is an
  >average or expectation value of a system which, as David
  >indicated, oscillates between positive and negative energy
  >states. Classical zero is a unique true vacuum state where
  >states of negative energy can have no meaning. Quantum zero is,
  >in general, a _false-vacuum_ state that can have different
  >values, and positive quantities can indeed be thought of as
  >"holes in nothing" because nothing is redefined as a rational
  >state.
  Thanks for pointing out this distinction Martin. The
  "nothingness" I have been alluding to is indeed a different
  animal than the quantum vacuum. The quandary in the meaning of,
  and the relationship between, Everything and Nothing, certainly
  predates quantum theory, and I submit that the latter has not
  substantially illuminated the issue, any more than general
  relativity has illuminated the fundamental nature of time.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m07-007.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:05]
Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science


  <snip>
  >However the irony is that long after Planck and the subjugation
  >of the troublesome infinities in the original QED theory, the
  >whole question of infinity sneaks in again through an
  >unsecurely-locked backdoor of the same quantum theory, which is
  >the "measurement problem". Popular Everett-style approaches to
  >"solving" the measurement problem, by proliferating an infinite
  >number of "observers" collapsing wavefunctions in an infinite
  >number of orthogonal worlds each with its own identical
  >measurement problem, have brought in an "ultraviolet
  >catastrophe" infinitely larger (in the Cantorian set-of-sets
  >sense) than the classical infinite-energy catastrophe that QED
  >was invented to cure in the first place!
  >The huge irony of this seems often to be lost on us. The only
  >"improvement" is that a number equal to infinity-minus-one of
  >these other worlds is to be forever unobservable. Planck may as
  >well have "solved" the cavity radiation problem in 1900 by
  >saying that there really is infinite energy inside the cavity,
  >but it must have gone into other dimensions. Thus he could have
  >"saved the phenomena" for classical physics without needing to
  >go to the trouble of founding quantum theory at all.
  >If we accept that we are observing only one instance of a
  >transfinite set of universes representing all possible states of
  >all possible physical systems obeying all possible variations of
  >all possible physical laws, then we can have infinity back - if
  >we want it. I'm not convinced that we do, and prefer to think
  >that there may be a more economical (and less anthropocentric)
  >solution of the measurement problem than infinite numbers of
  >"observers". When this is finally worked out I like to think
  >that the vaccum will be differently understood yet again, and
  >that taming it will involve an understanding of QG that
  >radically changes how we think not only about spacetime but
  >about quantum theory itself, and even the meaning and origin of
  >what we call probabilities.
  I must agree there is a profound lack of economy in the Many
  Worlds interpretation, although on the other hand, the 'collapse
  of the wave function' has always struck me as absurd on its
  face. I must conclude that we just don't get it yet, and it will
  have to suffice that the theory is predictive. Interpretation
  can wait for another day.
  It might be considered an appealing feature of the Everett model
  that it addresses the enormity of what may comprise Everything
  (in the grand sense of all that is not Nothing, rather than the
  more narrow sense of fluctuations in the quantum vacuum).
  However, it is not comprehensive in that regard, e.g., it does
  not (as I gather) allow spontaneous variations in universal
  constants or other 'non-physical' behavior, although it admits
  infinitely many individually 'well-behaved' universes.
  I am not completely averse to the idea that existence is
  quantized rather than a continuum, and perhaps consists only of
  a finite number of states (or a countably infinite number of
  them). But if so, the terse and unavoidable conclusion would
  seem to be: there's no such thing as nothing. I find the
  implications of that fairly creepy, with distinctly religious
  overtones.
  So, the result of all this philosophical waterboarding is that I
  have chronic headaches, have become a heavy drinker, and am soon
  to become a church-goer as well! I am now resolved to abandon
  this thread. Good luck.
  Mike

  Agreed, Martin. You have correctly exposed my sleight of hand in
  ramming three different concepts (The quantum zero point,
  classical zero, and the broader logico-philosophical idea of

  they were identical. Having admitted that, I'm still left with a
  sense of discomfort, perhaps based on the suspicion that the
  stochastic zero of quantum theory is a concept that can't be


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m07-008.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:06]
Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

  altogether separated from the absolute zero of nothingness. If
  nothing else, they share a common logical heritage. What
  fascinates me about all this is the way that, whatever course
  (conceptual framework) is adopted, it always seems that
  intractable difficulties are encountered if the logic is
  followed through far enough. To me, this is a surefire
  indication that something is fundamentally wrong with the
  conceptual framework - whether it be axioms, arguments or the
  whole process, we just don't know. Your splendidly condensed
  outline of the issues illustrates the point rather well.
  >Infinity and infinitesimals have the problem of leading to
  >catastrophe when introduced into calculations about real states,
  >but fortunately, despite the famous "unreasonable effectiveness"
  >of maths in producing entities that represent actuality, there
  >doesn't seem to be any clear physical basis for these ideas. In
  >classical physics any finite quantity at all can be infinitely
  >differentiated, but in electromagnetic theory this leads to the
  >ultraviolet catastrophe (equipartition of energy modes in cavity
  >radiation) and has to be replaced by a quantum principle, as is
  >well known. But what isn't quite so well known is that once
  >introduced here the quantum principle is forced to run through
  >the whole of physics to its spacetime foundations. If the energy
  >of spacetime is classically differentiable than quantum theory
  >fails for all other forces, because all other forces interact
  >through gravity. This is at the heart of why the search for
  >quantum gravity (QG) is such a big deal.
  >But many discussions of quantum spacetime proceed as though
  >there is a real differentiable continuum background underneath
  >the quantisation. This has been one of the major problems of
  >string theories for many years.
  Isn't that an inevitable problem, though? I don't mean in the
  historical sense, where habits of thought die hard - and why
  shouldn't they, if they've got us this far? Perhaps it runs a
  lot deeper. In effect, we are always having to build theoretical
  frontiers using the tools we have got, and until we reach the
  final frontier (assuming there is one - an assumption that I
  can't quite see the justification for until we get there) we
  can't have a solid basis for believing in the validity of those
  tools. If that is true, then it seems that there will always be
  examples of speculative work that can be shown to stand in
  contradiction to the methods whereby they are derived.
  >The true QG theory will be
  >radically quantised, and the notion of initesimal scale
  >(infinitesimal gravitational potentials) will not appear in it.
  >I tend to think that infinite scales (infinite gravitational
  >potentials) must also be unphysical, and that therefore all
  >possible physical states inside the universe will be
  >representable as finite relations amongst a finite number of
  >discrete elements.
  Is that right? Is it a mathematical issue or a physical one? I'm
  asking because I don't know. I might not be clear about the
  definitional basis for 'relation' and 'discrete element' here.
  It's just that there is an old metaphysical argument that
  derives the infinite from the finite that might apply: you start
  with, say, three discrete elements, a, b, and c, and one type of
  relation, call it 'r' - so you can have arb, arc, and brc. But
  if those three are viewed as discrete elements in themselves,
  you now have six discrete elements, and the relations between
  them all, including new ones like ar(arb), now number fifteen,
  and so on ad infinitum, literally.
  Is this just another version of the many-worlds interpretation?
  Whether it is or not, it at least serves to lay bare my own
  prejudice in the matter: an obstinate conviction that no matter
  how strongly the theoretical doors and windows are barred,
  infinity will always find a way in. I don't believe that because
  I think that's the way the physical world actually works. I
  believe it because I think it is built into our theoretical
  apparatus at a hopelessly deep, perhaps currently unanalysable,
  level.
  >This would mean that there is a finite number
  >of configurations of these elements, a finite number of
  >discriminable universe-states, and thus a finite probability of
  >occurrence of any given state (though not necessarily a finite
  >probability of re currence). Logical paradoxes involving


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m07-008.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:06]

  >infinite numbers of antithetical states all having probabilities

  >and that seems desirable.
  >However the irony is that long after Planck and the subjugation
  >of the troublesome infinities in the original QED theory, the
  >whole question of infinity sneaks in again through an
  >unsecurely-locked backdoor of the same quantum theory, which is

  >The huge irony of this seems often to be lost on us. The only

  >these other worlds is to be forever unobservable.
  I'm starting to feel like a kill-joy, a true pedant. While I
  agree with what you are saying here, I am compelled to point out
  that infinity-minus-one is still infinity. So the improvement is
  less than infinitesimal. It's not your fault Martin, it's the
  conceptual apparatus.
  >Planck may as
  >well have "solved" the cavity radiation problem in 1900 by
  >saying that there really is infinite energy inside the cavity,
  >but it must have gone into other dimensions. Thus he could have
  >"saved the phenomena" for classical physics without needing to
  >go to the trouble of founding quantum theory at all.
  >If we accept that we are observing only one instance of a
  >transfinite set of universes representing all possible states of
  >all possible physical systems obeying all possible variations of
  >all possible physical laws, then we can have infinity back - if
  >we want it. I'm not convinced that we do,
  I'm sure you are right, and I'm equally certain that most
  physicists would be glad to see it dead and buried. At the same
  time, as I've already indicated, I'm not at all sure that we'll
  ever be able to get rid of it, or, for that matter its
  troublesome reciprocal.
  >and prefer to think
  >that there may be a more economical (and less anthropocentric)
  If less anthropocentric, then I'll try to suspend my infinity
  prejudice and I'll queue to buy.
  >solution of the measurement problem than infinite numbers of

  That final point about 'the meaning and origin of what we call
  probabilities' intrigues me deeply. It is an aspect of the whole
  question (I mean that of the conceptual framework(s) used in
  frontier physics for the past, what, hundred years nearly?) that
  has been bothering me for ages. I think you hit the nail right
  on the head when you suggest that a final working out of
  QG/Spacetime/QT can't leave our understanding of probability
  untouched. My own amateur armchair hunch is that connections
  between Ramsey theory, entropy and extreme macroscopic systems
  will play a prominent role in whatever straightening out occurs.
  It would be most interesting, though, to hear more of your own
  ideas on the matter.
  I'm hoping that you will be prepared to say more, because I
  frequently feel quite distressed over some of the discussion of
  frontier physics that goes on in ufological circles. If the
  best-informed players don't come to the party it can only get
  worse.

                                           At Last The Truth About Little Green Men
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Mon, 07 Jan 2008 08:48:29 -0500
  Archived: Mon, 07 Jan 2008 08:48:29 -0500
  Subject: At Last The Truth About Little Green Men



  Source: The Daily Telegraph - London, UK
  http://tinyurl.com/yp2q76
  07/01/2008
  At Last, The Truth About Little Green Men
  By Jim White
  There used to be a feature in one of the Sunday newspapers
  called "The Expert's Expert". It asked people in different walks
  of life to nominate the person they most admired in their own
  profession. One week it might be chefs' favourite chef, the next
  the newsreaders' newsreader, although latterly in its lifespan
  it was more often the Celebrity B Listers' Celebrity B Lister.
  What a shame the item is no longer published. Because we are
  about to get a full airing of something many of us have waited
  years for: the conspiracy theorists' conspiracy theory of
  choice. This is the one at the root of them all, the granddaddy
  of paranoid investigation, the apparent establishment cover-up
  that has seized the imagination of thousands for a generation,
  the one that, by comparison, makes the death of Diana, Princess
  of Wales look as transparent as a back-lit cotton dress. The
  Ministry of Defence has unexpectedly announced that, under the
  30-year rule, it is to release the files from its D155
  intelligence branch, the unit charged with investigating UFO
  sightings.
  What news this is: we will discover exactly what was found in
  the official inquiry into the more than 7,000 UFO sightings
  registered across three decades of flying saucery. These are
  nothing less than Britain's own X Files, and within them will be
  found some of the high-water marks of alien contact. We will
  discover what happened in May 1977 when the crew of an RAF
  Vulcan flying over the Atlantic had a close encounter with an
  unexplained cigar-shaped object at 43,000 feet. And we will
  learn what lay behind the infamous Rendlesham incident in 1980,
  in which several witnesses reported seeing a craft decorated in
  hieroglyphics landing in Norfolk and depositing aliens into the
  countryside.
  The belief in regular contact with beings from outer space
  developed in post-war Britain into something of a secular
  religion. It has its own belief systems, its own certainties. At
  the heart of the credo is the conviction that successive
  governments are somehow wrapped up in all this: they have known
  what was going on and covered it up for their own purposes. The
  most common explanation for government action is that they were
  trying to adapt alien technology to keep one step ahead in the
  arms race.
  So ingrained has the conspiracy theory become that whole sub-
  sects have grown up around it. I once attended the British
  premi=E8re of Communion, a film about alien abduction, to which
  the publicity people had cunningly invited a dozen or so folk


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m07-009.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:08]
At Last The Truth About Little Green Men

  who claimed they had been whisked into space by creatures from
  another place. One woman earnestly informed me that there was a
  simple reason why the government was keeping quiet about the
  level of alien contact: the aliens were controlling senior
  members of the Cabinet. I asked if she had any evidence for this
  and she told me, without flinching, that on one of her regular
  trips aboard a visiting UFO she had seen the home secretary
  having his brain rewired. At the time the home secretary was Ken
  Clarke, about as grounded a politician as you can imagine, so it
  seemed unlikely to me. Obviously, if she'd seen John Redwood
  that would have been a different story.
  At first, the government denied D155 even existed, which hardly
  dampened the furious speculation. But now, infuriated by the
  refusal of the belief in collusion to go away, the MoD has
  decided to release the files in order to undermine what its
  spokesman called "the maze of rumour and frequently ill-informed
  speculation". It will, of course, do no such thing. The joy
  about a conspiracy theory is that denial is regarded as further
  proof of complicity. As Joe McGonagle, the UFO researcher, put
  it on hearing of the files' disclosure: "There will always be a
  hard core who believe that these files were prepared for release
  and that there is a secret department within the military which
  has a separate stash of files that have not been disclosed."
  I suppose it is possible. Just as it might have been energy from
  alien craft rather than a couple of pranksters with planks of
  wood that used to make all those crop circles. Though I can't
  see it. If governments have largely failed over the generations
  to control things like the economy, education and health, I
  doubt they could have been on top of evidence about contact with
  a superior race of beings. If nothing else, they would have
  misplaced all the data about their identity years ago.

  04 Jan 2008
  [Image]

  New Cornish UFO Sighting Pic
  By Antonella Lazzeri
  Britain is turning into an alien nation according to Sun readers
  who have flooded us with reports of UFO sightings.
  Following our story of a UFO seen off Cornwall on December 29 we
  were inundated by calls from people who had similar things all
  over the country.
  Some claimed they had seen alien spacecraft off the same bay in
  Cornwall where our original UFO was snapped.
  A man who asked just to be called Edward snapped a strange
  shaped object which appeared to be 'buzzing' a Navy ship.
  He said: "I was taking photos of the ship when a helicopter from
  it took off, flew west then landed back on board just a few
  minutes later.
  "It was only when I blew up the photos on my computer that I
  realised what the helicopter had gone off to take a look at.
  "It was in the exact same bay as the one featured in The Sun
  earlier this week." American holidaymaker Ian Mulford also
  believes he snapped a UFO at virtually the same spot as Edward.
  Ian said: "I was taking photographs and did not see anything
  unusual at the time, but after reviewing the pictures I found
  something very unusual in the background of a picture of one of
  the family.
  ‘ It didn't look like any normal aircraft so I am sure it is a
  UFO ’
  Partygoer Rodga Harvey claims he snapped a UFO as he made his
  way home from a party on New Years eve.
  Rodga, from St.Ives, said:"It was only when I looked at the
  photo later that I realised there was this weird flying object
  in the sky.
  "It didn't look like any normal aircraft so I am sure it is a
  UFO."
  Mum of one Rachel Clarke, 25, is totally convinced that she
  filmed two UFOs flying above the skies above Borehamwood on New
  Year's Day.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m07-012.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:09]

  Rachel said: "I was standing on the balcony of a neighbour's
  house celebrating.
  "We suddenly saw a bright light appear in the sky, then another
  one joined it.
  "They both started darting about really fast. They weren't
  flying around like normal planes, or helicopters.
  "Everyone who saw them, and there were about 15 of us, were
  amazed. I didn't see any green men flying them, but I am sure
  they were UFOs.
  Grandmother Mary Booth, 57, says she saw what she believes was a

Mystery Of P-51 Crash Goes Way Of Cold War




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena

    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 7

                                       Mystery Of P-51 Crash Goes Way Of Cold War
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Mon, 07 Jan 2008 09:05:01 -0500
  Archived: Mon, 07 Jan 2008 09:05:01 -0500
  Subject: Mystery Of P-51 Crash Goes Way Of Cold War



  Source: Elizabethtown News Enterprise - Elizabethtown, Kentucky, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/2gmfft
  Sunday, January 6, 2008

  Mystery Of P-51 Crash Goes The Way Of The Cold War
  FORT KNOX - Sure there’s a UFO, a space beam and a hush-hush
  government project - but this is mainly a story about timing.
  First, it was 60 years ago today that Capt. Thomas Mantell died
  while chasing what, at the time, was a UFO.
  Second, his close encounter happened six months to the day after
  a "flying saucer" crashed at a Roswell, N.M., ranch. Americans
  were gaga over green men.
  Third, Mantell and his P-51 Mustang fighter squadron happened to
  enter the Army post’s airspace at about the same time as the
  UFO, which reports say looked like a white ice cream cone with a
  glowing red tip.
  The supervisor at Godman Airfield tower that afternoon asked
  Mantell for an obvious favor: If you’ve got enough fuel, would
  you mind checking this out for us?
  Space travelers aside, the Cold War was getting really chilly
  and there was no telling what the Soviets were up to. Add to the
  mix the fact that Mantell, flying for the Kentucky Air National
  Guard, was a decorated World War II pilot.
  He obviously felt the investigation important enough to risk his
  own life, said Frank John Reid, a historical consultant for the
  Center for UFO studies in Chicago.
  So Mantell set off pretty much alone, pushing his plane far
  beyond what it was designed to do.
  Before he crashed, he managed to describe to those at the tower
  what appeared to be a "metallic object" of "tremendous size,"
  which varied in speed between about 180 to more than 300 mph,
  according to testimony of the airport’s chief operator posted on
  the Web site of the National Investigations Committee on Aerial
  Phenomena.
  When Mantell had positioned himself directly behind and slightly
  below the UFO, he uttered his final communication: "I am trying
  to close in for a better look."
  The chase had drawn him to 20,000 feet or higher. Above 10,000
  feet, a pilot in that kind of plane would need supplemental
  oxygen, said Lt. Col. Tim Moore, a state representative and
  member of the Kentucky Air National Guard.
  Mantell - who didn’t have this resource (a problem that could


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m07-013.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:10]
Mystery Of P-51 Crash Goes Way Of Cold War

  explain why he thought the object sped up so much) - passed out
  and his plane plunged to the ground south of Bowling Green.
  The incident received a lot of media coverage and myths about it
  sprouted up. For instance, rumor has it Mantell saw windows on
  the craft, and his wrecked plane had strange holes as if some
  sort of laser beam had shot it down.
  What happened, exactly, wasn’t made clear until quite a few
  years after the encounter, Reid said.
  Most now agree the object was a balloon. Specifically, Reid
  believes it was a Skyhook balloon the Navy had launched the day
  before in Minnesota. Operation Skyhook was a secret initiative
  to collect atmospheric data and put spy cameras over the Soviet
  Union, Reid said.
  While Reid is quick to give a terrestrial explanation of
  Mantell’s sighting, he "wobbles" about whether we ever have been
  visited by an intelligence beyond our own.
  Regardless of what Mantell saw, the fact it led to his death
  darkened our views of UFOs.
  "It was a very sobering incident," Reid said.
  It also is a story still repeated by those who venture into the
  sky - "kind of a unique footnote in the history of the Kentucky
  Air National Guard," Master Sgt. Tim Gagnon said.
  John Friedlein can be reached at 505-1746, or at
  jfriedlein.nul

  07 January 2008
  Residents Line Up To Confirm UFO Sightings
  By Petra Barnby
  More and more people are claiming they saw UFOs in Flintshire
  during the Christmas period.
  Last week, the Leader reported on the sighting, made by Harry
  Hughes, of Mynydd Isa, as he was going out to his shed on
  Christmas Day.
  Mr Hughes saw several orange-red orbs moving "faster than a
  plane" through the air, and glowing in the night sky. The
  incident matched a sighting over Wrexham last year.
  Now, three more reports have come in from people saying they saw
  the same objects on the same day.
  David Clark, of Elwy Close in Bryn y Baal, says he can confirm
  that everything Mr Hughes says is correct.
  He said: "It is absolutely true what he says. There were three
  very bright lights which suddenly separated and one looked like
  it shot straight up at high speed.
  "At first we thought they were balloons or planes but they were
  going too fast and they didn't look like planes.
  "There was no noise whatsoever and they were going so fast. I
  have never seen anything like it before."
  We published the story of the latest incident on our website,
  and users have flocked to view the details.
  A Mrs Coulton, from Mold, described how her family were left
  perplexed after seeing orange coloured lights.
  She said: "The light was a fair way off, it was coming towards
  us then stopped went backwards, stayed still for about four or
  five minutes, then faded away. It was really strange. It was
  definitely there, was not a firework, star, helicopter, or
  plane. We really don't know what it was."
  Marie Davies, of Chester Road in Mold, was driving from Holywell
  to Halykn on Christmas day when she spotted a red light low in
  the sky at 7pm.
  She said: "At first I thought it was the moon but it was too low
  in the sky. It was flame red and was standing still over the Dee
  Estuary way.

  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>

  Subject: You Are Not Alone



  Source: The Miami New Times - Florida,USA
  http://blogs.miaminewtimes.com/riptide/2008/01/you_are_not_alone.php
  Mon Jan 07, 2008
  You Are Not Alone
  by Elvis Ramirez
  "The people here are serious people. They're sincere [about
  their interest in the subject]", said Alicia Quaini, one of the
  members of the Fort Lauderdale-Miami UFO Group.
  The group gets together to watch videos dealing with UFOs and
  the conspiracies that surround them. The event is very low key,
  probably because most of the group's members are elderly.
  However, these aren't old folk gathering on a Saturday just
  because they had nothing else to do (some of them did seem like
  it though). After the event was over, many people stayed and sat
  around two tables pushed together to discuss not only the video
  but the news they had seen. They also discussed what they
  believed to be solutions to some of the world's issues. One
  woman even mentioned Nikola Tesla's perpetual energy coil as a
  solution to the energy crisis.
  Normally, if someone said things like that in any other venue,
  they would be labeled a nut job.
  The group was started by LeRoy D. Lawhorn after he realized that
  there was some demand for a place where people can talk openly
  about their experiences and beliefs about UFOs. Lawhorn claims
  to have seen a UFO during his days as a commercial pilot. "I saw
  that and thought, 'This is the real thing'," said Lawhorn.
  The event isn't the most exciting thing you can do on a Saturday
  afternoon. In fact, it is rather dull if you aren't interested
  in the subject. There isn't anything particularly special about
  it, but the fact that it is a group of people getting together
  to talk about a shared belief makes the experience something
  different.
  If you're looking for something akin to a science-fiction
  convention then don't bother making the drive, but if you're
  interested in meeting people (some of them kooks) with a belief
  in UFOs or if you are simply curious go ahead and stop by
  Gateway Terrace in Fort Lauderdale. Who knows, maybe you'll bump
  into Dennis Kucinich.
  "We're spreading the message, and the message is a message of
  love," Quaini said. -- Elvis Ramirez
  The meetings take place the first Saturday of every month at
  1943 N.E. 6th Court. Bldg. T-105, Ft. Lauderdale, FL, 33304.

  Hi Gerald
  Without wanting to get too deeply embroiled, because we are in
  the realm of very difficult speculations for which this is
  perhaps not the place (and because I'm not certain enough of my
  own ground to do more than speculate), the point that I'd wished
  to make was that although infinite and infinitesimal quantities
  are, I agree, paradoxical, there doesn't seem to be any clear
  requirement that these mathematical entities must correspond to
  physical ones, and some evidence (in the form of the success of
  quantum and quantum-inspired discretist approaches to physics)
  that they do not. There may even of course be pure mathematical
  discoveries in future that transform or subvert the notion of
  infinity and remove the "problem".
  That's not to say that we will be able to do without these
  entities in modelling nature, but it's quite possible. There
  might be a good reason for the fact that we are baffled by them,
  as by the notion of a probability greater than 1.0 or the
  concept of a "blue smell". An infinite set might turn out to be
  a concept that is impossible to define meaningfully in any
  physical terms, just as the concept of an infinitesimal interval
  of real space has no physical correlative.in the quantum Planck
  regime. Another analogy might be the fact that a local-real
  velocity greater than c has no physical meaning for masses in SR
  spacetime.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m08-005.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:13]
Re: Parallel Universes Beguile Science

  These are not crude embargoes, because we know or can conjecture
  paradigms within which the regions of impossibility become
  confined as limit cases within a transcendent interpretation; so
  that displacement greater than c may be possible and the Planck
  regime may turn out to reveal a causal "hidden variable" of some
  kind. But the >c displacement will by definition not be a
  translation, and the <h variable will not (very probably) be a
  "fine graining" of real action. These are cases where the act of
  transcending the limit transforms the context, and as ever it is
  (paradoxically!) the triumph of transcendence that reveals the
  the original hope as quaintly inapt. It's possible that a new
  mathematical physics may redefine the meaning of an infinite set
  in the form of some functionally equivalent bounded operation
  that is formally free of the old difficulties, and it will
  become an idea digested and metabolised into unrecognisable
  forms, itself of interest only to historians like Newtonian
  absolute space or the giant turtles under the earth (well, a bit
  colourful, but you get the point)..
  As for the meaning and origin of probabilities, I have in mind a
  similar sort of process. In terms of the absolute determinism of
  Victorian science "chance" had a clear _operational_ meaning -
   unpredictability in practice - but no physical meaning because
  prediction of one particle's state from its interaction with
  another was always possible in principle. In terms of modern
  quantum theory "chance" has a clear _physical_ meaning - the
  probabilistic behaviour of particles - rather than a merely
  operational meaning, because such one-on-one prediction is _not_
  always possible in principle. But what now does it mean to say
  that chance underlies the world? Given all the talk of "god
  playing dice" one could be forgiven for supposing that we are
  allowing a moribund classical definition of chance to underpin
  quantum theory, which can't be right. In fact it must be that
  quantum theory redefines "chance".
  The unpredictable order of quantum actuality is not determined
  solely by the local past of every particle, but it _is_order
  nonetheless. When we say that events occur in accordance with
  rules of probability we are now saying: "These systematic
  distributions reflect certain unknown dimensions of the ordering
  of events in the world." In other words, to deny that an event
  is determined _may_ be the same as denying that it is
  contingent, but only when contingency is defined in terms of
  local-real histories; a system of non-local contingency may
  entirely negate the utility of the concept of determinism and
  yet still be very highly ordered and predictable to 14 decimal
  places.
  The radical rediscovery of randomness in quantum theory may be
  the very advance that in time entirely strips the concept of
  randomness from our scientific vocabulary, by deriving highly
  complex "pseudorandom" behaviour as a limit case of some mature
  meta-theory which explains in a radically new way _why_ the
  local-real order is statistical in nature. An analogy might be
  this: You can make a simple divided box out of strips of wood
  and pour dried peas into it in such a way that the normal
  distribution bell-curve results with a high degree of
  predictability. Presently we say that this merely illustrates a
  stochastic behaviour that "just is". Discovering that there is
  an analogous unseen causal structure or graining in the
  underlying nonlocal physics of the world could explain why
  matter orders itself via quantum electrodynamics into the wooden
  boxes and the dried peas in such a way as to producxe these
  scale-free regularities.
  That's where I suspect the answer is, and finding that structure
  will involve one day going beyond field theory and particles and
  forces in 4-space (or 10-space) to a completely new type of
  (projective) geometrical representation that allows the
  underlying map of gravitational actions to reify the indefinite-
  dimensional state space of quantum theory..
  Anyway, these are just vague personal intuitions (as I'm sure is
  all too obvious) so I'll leave it there. I now propose to join
  Mike for a dram or two in his licensed monastery :-)
  Last word to T. S. Elliot: "We shall not cease from exploration
  and the end of all our exploring will be to return back where we
  started and know the place for the first time."

  Consider this: how much sense can be made of the idea of a world
  (perhaps, in Martin's terminology, a 'radically quantised' one)
  where, as you put it, 'there's no such thing as nothing'? Surely
  we will always need a closely related family of concepts -

  etc. - to act, if nothing else, as a background reference point

  philosophers, logicians and physicists each adopted their own
  favoured formulation, none of which fully satisfied the
  conceptual requirements of the others?
  There would no longer be a nothing to put in the null set!
  We might consider turning to the physicists to settle the issue
  through a suitably verifiable 'theory of absolutely everything
  with nothing left out this time', but I seriously doubt that
  this would do the trick for mathematicians, for example, who
  would want to go on playing around with speculative systems that
  the physicists would be telling us must exist, but are
  unobservable.
  Whichever way we come at it, something's got to give. As it
  looks at the moment, at least in my clumsy little representation
  of the problem, it might even be verification that has to give
  way - no doubt to screams of protest from the philosophers who
  have grown accustomed to allowing everybody else to dirty their
  hands settling matters of empirical truth.

  UFO Club Calls It A Day
  By Ash Bolton
  First there was the sighting of the mysterious multi-coloured
  chandelier-shaped object hovering in the south's skies.
  Then there was the fast-moving bright light spotted over
  Beaulieu in the New Forest.
  And then, a few years later, there were the orange globes
  sailing above the rooftops of Hythe.
  These are all among the bizarre, odd and unexplained sightings
  of a group of UFO spotters monitoring the skies above Hampshire.
  But now, after almost 20 years of no definitive evidence and a
  few unanswered questions, they have decided to fold up their
  telescopes.
  With the help of sci-fi shows such as The X-Files, in the early
  1990s the popularity of hunting for extra-terrestrials was sky-
  high and Southampton UFO Group (SUFOG) boasted more than 75
  members.
  But since then there has been a wane in intergalactic interest
  and founding member Steve Gerrard has decided to shut the group
  down after only four members turned up to its last meeting.
  The group started in November 1990, when Steve put an advert in
  the back of the Daily Echo looking for extraterrestrial
  enthusiasts.
  Over the years their photos of strange objects in the sky have
  been splashed across the world's media, and the Ministry of
  Defence has even investigated their video footage.
  One of the original members, Ernie Sears, said the group has
  taken hundreds of photographs during their sky-watches, but said
  there was one incident that "changed his life forever".
  Ernie, 83, of Netley, said: "I had my first sighting in March
  1960 at Portsdown Hill. I saw a very strange-looking light in
  the sky. I thought it must be an aircraft with the sun
  reflecting off it. But it seemed to be hanging there and I
  thought: It can't be one of those pesky UFOs.' "Half an hour
  later I heard the roar of jet engines. I rushed to an opening
  and saw two Meteor jets flying low over Gosport, coming from the
  direction of Thorny Island Aerodrome.
  "To my amazement this object was still hanging in the sky in the


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m08-011.shtml[09/12/2011 23:51:17]
UFO Club Calls It A Day

  same place and not moving. I knew then that it wasn't an
  aircraft.
  "I watched as the jets neared it but as they did it turned on
  end and disappeared into the blue sky like a light being
  switched off.
  "I ran into a phone box and phoned Thorny Island Air Control. I
  asked him if he could tell me what the object was the Meteor
  Jets were chasing. I'll never forget his answer. He said: You
  did not see any object and you did not see any Meteor jets.'
  "Since then I have been convinced there is other life out there
  and I am determined to prove it's true."
