  The Sightings:
  1977
  Broad Haven, Wales
  There were several reported UFO sightings in the area during the
  1970s, but the most widely publicised was the strange visitation
  to a field near to Broad Haven Primary School in February 1977.
  Fourteen primary children witnessed a silvery yellow cigar
  shaped UFO and some said they had seen a figure in a silver suit.
  Following this report there were adult witnesses to a dome
  shaped UFO in the same area.

  1989
  Bonnybridge, Scotland
  A fire crew were attending a blaze when they saw what appeared
  to be a red object hovering in the distance. A second object
  then appeared above a loch about 20ft from the witnesses,
  followed by a third which passed overhead. After a further spate
  of sightings the area was dubbed the UFO Capital of Scotland.

  1987
  Ilkley Moor
  A former police officer was walking over moorland when he
  claimed he saw a small green creature about 4ft tall with
  overlong arms running towards a hollow in the hillside. He
  shouted at the creature, which waved its arms at him, and he
  managed to snap a picture. The resulting photograph, which
  experts later said had not been tampered with, did show a
  strange figure, but sadly he was never seen again.

Could Life Be Older Than Stars & Planets?




                                                          UFO Updates
                                    A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                                'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 22

                                            Could Life Be Older Than Stars & Planets?
  From: Ray Dickenson <r.dickenson.nul>
  Date: Tue, 22 Jan 2008 13:05:33 -0000
  Archived: Tue, 22 Jan 2008 08:12:49 -0500
  Subject: Could Life Be Older Than Stars & Planets?

  Hello List,
  Folk trying to work out probabilities of life in our galaxy (or
  in the universe) often refer to the Drake Equation, which uses
  the numbers (and ages) of planets in the Milky Way as basic
  factors.
  Why only look at planets? Because, as Gribbin et al show, life
  needs an energy gradient - from hot to cold say, to power the
  'work' of living. Being close to a star, organic molecules on a
  planet can use the star's radiation to start 'self-organizing'
  to greater complexity and 'life'. So on Earth we can find a
  chain: starting with photo-synthesis > plants > herbivores >
  carnivores & omnivores (us).
  Is there an energy source other than stars? Yes. The Cosmic
  Microwave Background (CMB), sometimes called the relic radiation
  from a putative 'big bang'. Yet it doesn't seem promising, for
  two reasons - i) it's only about 3 degrees above absolute zero
  and ii) it's all around, so where's the gradient?
  i) The temperature _is_ only 3 degrees now. But going back in
  time, it was hotter and hotter.
  ii) And the gradient? In deep space we find huge clouds of
  molecules, many of them organic molecules. The bigger the cloud
  the colder its interior will be, because outer layers will
  absorb the radiation - so there's your gradient. And it's an
  enclosed system - the energy gradient is internal to the cloud.
  Therefore clouds of molecules have had the energy input to do
  the 'work' of self-organizing. We could say that's obvious
  because some clouds' molecules are very complex - nucleic acids
  (predecessors of DNA) have been detected. And the further back
  you go, the more energy such clouds were receiving.
  How far back? Mainstream scientists who subscribe to the
  'redshift hypothesis' say the visible universe is only 15-20
  billion yrs old - although other scientists (Arp et al) say it
  could be much older (and bigger). That mainstream posits an
  evolution from primitive stars in galactic clouds of dust to
  regular stars (several main 'generations') in regular galaxies.
  Their problem is: as far as they can see, even 13 to 14 billion
  light-years away (that's distance _and_ time), there's only
  'regular' galaxies to be seen.
  So, if you believe the mainstream anyway, life could have
  evolved in deep space as far back as c. 14 - 19 billion years
  ago. If you examine other evidence (maybe check Halton Arp's
  'Seeing Red') then first life in the universe could be much,
  much older.
  Interstellar or deep-space forms of life, amorphous yet
  energetic, would certainly seem to match up with some of the
  things - "high pulsers" - that we see in NASA satellite and
  shuttle footages. Try 'video NASA UFO' in Google.

  Cheers

  Hi Everyone!
  With the great interest and continuing media coverage of the
  large UFO sighted by multiple witnesses in Stephenville, Texas,
  this has encouraged many others to report their own sightings of
  unusual or unexplained things in the sky which they would
  otherwise not report. This "UFO flyby" in Denton, Texas is just
  one such example.
  Although there were two witnesses making this UFO report more
  credible and useful to researchers, there are contradictions and
  interpretations that make this case difficult to evaluate. For
  example, the witnes (Lance Oliver) writes "...my wife, Mary, and
  I saw a fast moving object flyby OVERHEAD..." and then writes
  "...but appeared too low and big to be a shooting star...".
  Although no noise was heard by the witnesses, not unexpected
  considering they saw the UFO from inside their car, considering
  the duration, size (about the same angular size of the Moon) and
  colour of the sighting, this UFO can easily be explained as a
  fireball.
  Since this UFO was reported on January 21 just one day after it


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m23-006.shtml[09/12/2011 23:53:40]
Re: Denton UFO Flyby

  was sighted, there are no reports yet of bright fireballs seen
  in the sky over Texas by the North American Meteor Network.
  Of course, there are other possible explanations too for this
  very brief and unexpected UFO sighting. Considering the shape
  and colour of the UFO seen from their car moving in the same
  direction as the UFO, it could have been have been a startled
  bird flying in the car's headlights.
  Another possibility is that the UFO as depicted in the drawing
  that accompanied this article which makes it seem more saucer
  shaped than a chevron, was produced by a moving spotlight. There
  are currently four very bright moving searchlights in downtown
  Toronto whose beams are not visible but which do produce such
  saucer shapes on the cloud layer above the city (similar to the
  "UFO" I saw over New York City that was created by the very
  bright searchlights located at the WTC site after 9/11). The
  short duration of the UFO sighting in Denton, Texas can thus be
  easily explained by the "...partly cloudy..." sky conditions
  mentioned by the witness since a moving "UFO" would indeed seem
  to disappear when it entered a region of clear sky.
  What do we do with UFO reports such as the one above that have
  contradictory and insufficient information and which have many
  very likely prosaic explanations too? These should be added to a
  UFO database but I don't think they should be promoted in the
  media as further good examples that UFOs are real and not of
  this world (at least some of them) as many ufologists such as
  Stan Friedman, and myself, know they are.
  Too many very dubious and insignificate UFO incidents do little
  to arouse interest among the public or even encourage renewed
  scientific inquiry in order to finally come up with answers to
  this ongoing mystery but only serve to create doubts and cast
  further ridicule on all those involved, from witnesses to
  researchers, in this important field.

  Nick Balaskas

   Bill O'Reilly & Colleagues in the 'No Spin' Twilight Zone
   The full dimensions and level of media ignorance, laziness,
   plain stupidity, in reporting what has been going on in Texas
   skies is difficult to describe and fully catalogue without using
   hyperbole mixed with obscenities. If ever there was a legitimate
   excuse for scathing imprecation, and hot rhetoric, this is it.
   There are wondrous awesome powers in our skies. Powers that
   frolic freely, from ocean to earth orbit. From UK coast channels,
   to Arizona night skies. Power that was seen in awe by a
   commercial airline captain at 39,000 ft. wondering why whole

   object that could swallow an aircraft carrier blotted out the
   skies as it was filmed years ago, the results rushed into
   vaulted blackness.
   And in Texas skies massive gray shapes pocked with immaculate
   precision hung as if by colossal magic in ominous immensity and
   witnessed by enough tough clear eyed hunters, former pilots, and
   other sober observers to form a jury that could convict a lying
   government if subject to Jurisprudence.
   These same Texas citizens, witnessed what thousands have worried
   and wondered about, why are we seeing our military assets caught
   with hands in the intercept cookie jar, over and over as pilots
   are ordered to chase these lightning quick flying gray
   mountains?

   staff reporters and talking heads irredeemably half witted? Is
   there a real shred of fire and spark of plain anger or curiosity
   about what is going on? Where is the raw real curiosity, and a
   basic reporters sense that Texas size whoppers of lies and

  known some 20 years before. However, the 'blockbuster' was the
  claim that, starting in 1955, about 50% of the UFO sightings
  were actually sightings of the U-2 spyplane that started flying
  that summer.

  him why he wrote it. He responded that he only wrote what he had
  been told by the 'old-timers' who ran the U-2 and follow on
  spyplane programs.
  I told him he would get into trouble with ufologists and
  historians for writing as he did with no explanation, but his
  excuse was the same as for most historians:
  "I only write what others tell me", (and don't think for myself).

  In Tanabi, Sao Paulo State in Brazil, a witness who lives in a
  small hotel near a sugar cane field, heard a noise like the cane
  was breaking. He went to see what is was and told Globo TV that
  he saw a big UFO and found a big crop circle in the cane.

  laid to the right side and some to the left.

  impossible for the circle to be formed by wind action.

  TV that field machines couldn't make the circle.
  As there is one witness that saw an UFO, people believe that this
  crop circle was made by a UFO.

  case. A pity its in Portuguese, but will give you an idea of
  what happened in Tanabi yesterday.

                                                     Yreka UFO Sighting Reported
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 08:41:03 -0500
  Archived: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 08:41:03 -0500
  Subject: Yreka UFO Sighting Reported



  Source: Siskiyou Daily News - Yreka, California
  http://www.siskiyoudaily.com/articles/2008/01/22/news/5912208news2.txt
  Tuesday, January 22, 2008


  Possible UFO Sighting Reported
  By Brad Smith
  Daily News Staff Writer

  YREKA -- Stephenville, Tex., residents aren't the only ones
  reporting unidentified flying objects above their community. A
  few weeks ago, Yreka resident Mary Hay reportedly saw a strange
  aircraft fly above her while she was at the Valero gas station
  on South Main Street.
  According to Hay, she was purchasing some kerosene and saw
  something moving across the sky. It happened on Jan. 8, sometime
  around 8 p.m., she said.
  Describing the object as 'slightly wedge-shaped,' Hay said it
  had three rows of lights underneath it, the middle row longer
  than the others. The object flew from east to west, 'then
  disappeared very quickly,' she said.
  This is the first time that something like this has happened to
  Hay.
  Since her sighting, she has told some of her family, friends and
  co-workers. While some have scoffed at the notion of UFOs and
  aliens, others have told her that they have seen the same thing
  and that she shouldn't feel "weird" talking about it.
  'I didn't even know about the (Stephenville) Texas UFOs until a
  few days ago,' she said.
  According to the Associated Press, several people have reported
  seeing UFOs since Jan. 8. The sightings have made national news,
  even causing CNN's Larry King to do a show about them.
  Ruben Uriate, director for Northern California's Mutual UFO
  Network, said that Hay's sighting is 'one of many.'
  'There's been a spike in reports,' he said. He speculates that
  the Stephenville sightings have raised awareness and that
  'people are looking up at the skies, paying more attention.'
  Uriate said that Hay shouldn't feel uneasy talking about her
  claim. Many pilots, law enforcement and military personnel have
  stepped forward, he stated, reporting their experiences.
  For more information on reporting a possible UFO, check the
  Mutual UFO Network (www.mufon.com) and the National UFO
  Reporting Center (www.nuforc.org) Web sites.

                                                        Web Searching For UFOs
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 08:47:09 -0500
  Archived: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 08:47:09 -0500
  Subject: Web Searching For UFOs



  Source: The Fort Worth Star Telegram - Fort Worth, Texas, USA
  http://www.star-telegram.com/state_news/story/426612.html
  Wed, Jan. 23, 2008

  Searching For UFOs
  By Bryon Okada
  Star-Telegram Staff Writer
  Seems a lot of people went UFO-crazy last week.
  OK, it didn't top the Hannah Montana-to-Miley Cyrus midconcert
  switcheroo involving a body double, or the death of actor Brad
  Renfro, but the Erath County UFO craze topped everything else on
  the Internet last week.
  In the week ending Saturday, "UFO photos" was the No. 3 fastest-
  moving search term used on all Web sites, according to New York-
  based Hitwise, an online measurement company that ranks search
  terms based on relative change.
  Among news and media sites, "UFO sightings" was No. 4 of all
  searches in the U.S. "Texas UFO" was No. 5 and "UFO and Texas"
  was No. 9.
  "Obviously, search term behavior is a good indicator of what's
  on people's minds," said Matt Tatham, Hitwise media relations
  manager.
  And, of course, it was one of the most-read stories at www.star-
  telegram.com last week, too.

  Wed Jan 23, 2008

  F-16s Were In Area Where UFO Reported
  By Angela K. Brown,
  Associated Press Writer
  FORT WORTH, Texas - Fighter jets were training nearby the night
  dozens of Stephenville-area residents reported seeing a UFO this
  month, Air Force Reserve officials said Wednesday, backtracking
  on earlier statements.
  FORT WORTH, Texas - Fighter jets were training nearby the night
  dozens of Stephenville-area residents reported seeing a UFO this
  month, Air Force Reserve officials said Wednesday, backtracking
  on earlier statements.
  The announcement did little to satisfy residents of Texas dairy
  country who swear that what they saw in the sky Jan. 8 was no
  airplane. Some said it even bolstered their claims, because
  several people reported seeing at least two fighter jets chasing
  an object.
  "This supports our story that there was UFO activity in that
  area," said Kenneth Cherry, the Texas director of the Mutual UFO
  Network, which took more than 50 reports from locals at a
  meeting last weekend. "I find it curious that it took them two
  weeks to 'fess up. I think they're feeling the heat from the
  publicity."
  Officials at the Joint Reserve Base Naval Air Station in Fort
  Worth initially said none of their planes had been in the area,
  but on Wednesday they said 10 F-16s were there that day. The
  officials said they were mistaken and wanted to set the record
  straight "in the interest of public awareness."
  Maj. Karl Lewis, a spokesman for the 301st Fighter Wing at the
  base, declined to comment on the nature of the military training
  or say whether it took place on other days.
  Lewis had said earlier this month that residents might have seen
  an illusion caused by two commercial airplanes and reflections
  from the setting sun. On Wednesday, he said he should not have
  speculated about the reported sightings.
  =46rom well-respected business owners to a county constable,
  several dozen people say they saw a flying object that was
  larger, quieter, faster and lower to the ground than an
  airplane. They also said its lights changed configuration,
  unlike those of a plane.
  "I guarantee that what we saw was not a civilian aircraft,"


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m24-008.shtml[09/12/2011 23:53:47]
'F-16s Were In Area' Where UFO Reported

  Steve Allen, a pilot and freight company owner, said Wednesday.
  The planes' training area in the Brownwood Military Operating
  Area includes Stephenville's Erath County, but Allen said it
  does not include the airspace where he saw the object. Also,
  Jan. 8 was not the only day sightings were reported.
  Anne Frazor, who owns a fabric store in Stephenville, about 70
  miles southwest of Fort Worth, said many in town have seen
  military aircraft zoom overhead from time to time as part of
  training operations. But she said that wasn't what she saw Jan.
  8.
  "I couldn't begin to say what it was, but to me it wasn't
  planes," Frazor said.
  Since the reported sightings two weeks ago, the 17,000-resident
  city is having fun with the international publicity. Some high-
  schoolers made T-shirts depicting a flying saucer beaming up a
  cow with the messages: "Stephenville: the new Roswell" and
  "They're here for the milk!" Several stores put new messages on
  their marquees, including "Aliens welcome."
  This week Tarleton State University is even hosting a lecture by
  a UFO researcher on the U.S. government's secret response to
  UFOs, based on previously classified documents obtained under
  the Freedom of Information Act.
  The U.S. Air Force says it has not investigated UFO sightings
  since 1969 when it ended Project Blue Book, which examined more
  than 12,600 reported UFO sightings =97 including 700 that were
  never explained. That program started a few months after the
  1947 crash near Roswell, N.M., of an aircraft the government
  said was a top-secret weather balloon but others have claimed
  was an alien spacecraft.
  "What we want is the government to admit there are UFOs and what
  they know about them," Cherry said.

  Honorable Member of Congress
  As an elected official I want to draw your attention to a
  subject that can no longer be ignored. Remarkable evidence is

  our planet. I know this information sounds unbelievable but
  please keep an open mind.

  has been accumulated by two disclosure initiatives. These 460

  witnesses possess the ranks of Brigadier Generals, Commander of
  ICBM Launch facilities, Senior FAA Crash Site Investigators,
  astronauts, pilots and officers with above top secret clearance.
  This testimony is only the tip of the iceberg.
  Other governments have started releasing previously classified
  data on ETs and UFOs. France was the first, in March 2007 the
  French National Space Agency placed 1600 previously classified
  UFO sighting reports into the public domain for examination;
  beginning the process of full disclosure of non-Earth origin
  craft. Similarly, the United Kingdom in May 2007 began a
  disclosure initiative. Other countries have started to follow
  suit. It is time for the United States to do the same.
  The United Nations General Assembly voted to inviting U.N.
  Member States "to take appropriate steps to coordinate on a
  national level scientific research and investigation into
  extraterrestrial life, including unidentified flying objects,
  and to inform the Secretary-General.=94
  The Honorable Paul Hellyer, a former Canada's Defense Minister
  and Deputy Prime, stated publicly in September 2005 at the
  University of Toronto=92s Convocation Hall before the press and
  over 500 people, "UFOs, are as real as the airplanes that fly
  over your head."
  Colonel Phillip J. Corso, a highly decorated retired U.S. Army
  Intelligence officer, who had direct contact with, and was in
  charge of material from crashed extraterrestrial vehicles.
  Colonel Corso=92s documentation is supported by a retired American
  four star General as being, =93true and even more=85=94
  In my personal experience, I was a U.S. Army Major and held a

  Scientist and am a graduate of the U.S. Army Computer Science

                                                          UFOs Beyond Reason?
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 14:49:46 -0500
  Archived: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 14:49:46 -0500
  Subject: UFOs Beyond Reason?



  Source: The West Linn Tidings
  http://tinyurl.com/3586dg
  Jan 24, 2008

  UFOs: Beyond Reason?
  Will the world ever know the truth about UFOs? A West Linn
  ufologist, Keith Rowell, hopes so - he'd also like to know
  By Nicole DeCosta
  The West Linn Tidings
  It was a sunny day in 2006.
  No clouds.
  A light wind peaked at 10 mph.
  West Linn resident Keith Rowell stepped outside his house to
  find a strange luminescent blue, white and red spherical object
  drifting through the sky. Sensing that this cluster wasn't just
  an escapee batch of party balloons, he ran inside to grab his
  video camera, zoomed in and hit "record." Six seconds later, the
  battery died.
  Ten years prior, Rowell witnessed golden yellow and cobalt blue
  spheres in the sky above him while visiting a friend in Lake
  Oswego.
  UFOs?
  Rowell is an investigator of sorts - a ufologist, boots on the
  ground, visiting people's houses, asking questions and taking
  measurements.
  "I've always had an interest in mysteries of the real world -
  not so much interested in the fictional mysteries," Rowell said.
  But that was before discovering books on unidentified flying
  objects while working for Portland Public Schools in 1974.
  "I was an open minded skeptic," Rowell said.
  So, he started reading.
  Three decades later, Rowell's basement is out of this world - in
  size and subject matter.
  Hundreds of books about UFOs, sorted by author, line the
  perimeter of the room, with overflow space and alien memorabilia
  in the adjoining den, where he updates his Web site for MUFON -
  Mutual UFO Network, Inc. Rowell serves as the assistant state
  director for Oregon MUFON. He retired from technical writing
  about three years ago.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m24-011.shtml[09/12/2011 23:53:48]
UFOs Beyond Reason?

  "I wrote computer manuals that everybody hates to read," he
  said.
  Now, he updates the Oregon MUFON Web site, "to give people a
  reasoned voice of how to look into and study UFOs. It's a jungle
  out there," he said.
  When asked about the recent UFO sightings in Texas which the
  Texas chapter of MUFON is investigating, Rowell just shrugged
  his shoulders.
  MUFON is a national organization with an emphasis on scientific
  investigation and analysis of UFO events, while promoting
  knowledge for the public about what is currently known about
  UFOs, according Rowell. Rowell is certified to investigate these
  phenomena that both mesmerize and scare the public.
  Rowell said that the subjects of UFOs is controversial and
  emotional. When investigating paranormal activity - crop
  circles, cattle mutilations, UFO claims and other bizarre
  happenings - he said many people don't understand what happened
  but want an answer. And many feel relieved to hear it may be a
  meteor that caught their eye in the sky.
  Hoaxes happen every so often with the increase of Internet use
  and ability to quickly report things, he said.
  "The 'keystroke hoax' is common now in Oregon because we have
  one person who is doing this from downstate Oregon," he said,
  meaning someone is repeatedly reporting false UFO sightings.
  But debunkers, Rowell said, are destructive.
  "Alternative medicine, UFOs, religious beliefs - this kind of
  person never accepts any amount of evidence," he said.
  Rowell earned a degree in philosophy and librarianship. He now
  acts like a live history reporter, speaking nonchalantly in
  public and private about Project Blue book - the Air Force's
  official investigation of UFOs in the 1950s and 1960s.
  He suggests that others read about John Mack, M.D., a
  psychiatrist and professor at Harvard who is considered to be a
  leading authority on the transformational effects of alleged
  alien encounter experiences.
  Rowell said that there are two obstacles holding the public from
  understanding UFOs - national security and the paranormal world.
  "We live in a national security state since 1947 when the
  National Security Act created the CIA," he said.
  U.S. Government forces protect the interests of its people.
  Thus, the UFO subject is very hush, hush, he said.
  "The fear of public panic about the reality of little alien
  bodies on ice and parts of saucers in storage gives our national
  security state pause about revealing the truth about UFOs,"
  Rowell said.
  He continued, "They are also trying to 'back engineer' the
  artifacts that they have to turn these engineering insights into
  human designed military weapons."
  The Roswell UFO incident - involving the recovery of materials
  near Roswell, N.M. in 1947 - is still under speculation. Were
  the remains really that of an alien craft or a secret research
  balloon, such as the U.S. military said?
  Small, round flying objects referred to as Foo Fighters followed
  allied bombers over Germany during WWII. Sometimes they would
  appear in clusters. Witnesses often assume that they were
  weapons employed by the enemy. Later it was found out that
  neither side had anything to do with them and the case remains
  unexplained, according to Wikipedia.org.
  Delving further back in time, the 1939 fictional adaptation of
  the science fiction novel "The War of the Worlds" radio
  broadcast fooled listeners of a Martian invasion on earth and
  caused mass panic.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m24-011.shtml[09/12/2011 23:53:48]
UFOs Beyond Reason?

  "UFOs are bound up with the paranormal world - psychic stuff:
  ghosts, telepathy, near death experiences, Big Foot, the Lock
  Ness Monster," Rowell said.
  He said that those at MUFON hope to help others deepen their
  understanding of UFOs by working through the various sides of,
  "the UFO question."
  Rowell said that sophisticated business people and common folk
  have reported seeing UFOs.
  According to the UFOCAT Web site and Rowell, more than 1,000
  potential UFO sightings occurred in Oregon between 1947 and
  1980.
  MUFON operates off donations, from people like Rowell who donate
  $50 a year.
  "You cannot get funds from foundations, the U.S. government and
  other sources of ordinary funding because it's a 'non-subject,'
  meaning 'not real' so it doesn't get time, money or expertise,"
  he said. "It's frustrating."
  Rowell hopes that someday MUFON gets some serious money to aid
  with investigations and informing the public.
  "Millions and millions of dollars," he said. "We just want to
  get the word out. 'It concerns me that our society as a whole
  doesn't know what I believe to be the truth."
  The Oregon MUFON Web site invites opinions because opinions are,
  "stronger than an impression and less strong than positive
  knowledge."
  Rowell's wife, Jan Rowell, seems to have a typical American
  viewpoint on the concept of UFOs.
  "Who knows," she said. "It's just one of those things. Ask
  Keith, he's the expert."
  Rowell said that sometime he'd like the public to lighten their
  grip dubbing UFOs as a crazy idea and irrelevant and have the
  government reveal their secrets.
  "Right now I," Rowell said, "unfortunately, am your expert."
  For more information about Keith Rowell and MUFON, visit
  http://oregonmufon.com

                                             Military Fails To Halt Speculation On UFOs
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 14:52:38 -0500
  Archived: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 14:52:38 -0500
  Subject: Military Fails To Halt Speculation On UFOs



  Source: The Detroit News - Michigan, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/2xnx9h
  Thursday, January 24, 2008

  Military Fails To Halt Speculation On UFOs
  Angela K. Brown
  Associated Press
  FORT WORTH, Texas -- Fighter jets were training nearby the night
  dozens of Stephenville-area residents reported seeing a UFO this
  month, Air Force Reserve officials said Wednesday, backtracking
  on earlier statements.
  The announcement did little to satisfy residents of Texas dairy
  country who swear that what they saw in the sky Jan. 8 was no
  airplane. Some said it even bolstered their claims, because
  several people reported seeing at least two fighter jets chasing
  an object.
  "This supports our story that there was UFO activity in that
  area," said Kenneth Cherry, the Texas director of the Mutual UFO
  Network, which took more than 50 reports from locals at a
  meeting last weekend. "I find it curious that it took them two
  weeks to 'fess up. I think they're feeling the heat from the
  publicity."
  Advertisement click here
  Officials at the Joint Reserve Base Naval Air Station in Fort
  Worth initially said none of their planes had been in the area,
  but on Wednesday they said 10 F-16s were there that day. The
  officials said they were mistaken and wanted to set the record
  straight "in the interest of public awareness."
  Maj. Karl Lewis, a spokesman for the 301st Fighter Wing at the
  base, declined to comment on the nature of the military training
  or say whether it took place on other days.
  Lewis had said earlier this month that residents might have seen
  an illusion caused by two commercial airplanes and reflections
  from the setting sun. On Wednesday, he said he should not have
  speculated about the reported sightings.
  From well-respected business owners to a county constable,
  several dozen people say they saw a flying object that was
  larger, quieter, faster and lower to the ground than an
  airplane. They also said its lights changed configuration,
  unlike those of a plane.
  "I guarantee that what we saw was not a civilian aircraft,"
  Steve Allen, a pilot and freight company owner, said Wednesday.
  The planes' training area in the Brownwood Military Operating
  Area includes Stephenville's Erath County, but Allen said it


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m24-012.shtml[09/12/2011 23:53:49]
Military Fails To Halt Speculation On UFOs

  does not include the airspace where he saw the object.

                                                     ET Life Or A Man On Mars?
  From: Franklin D. Fields <fields.nul>
  Date: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 09:23:33 -0500 (EST)
  Archived: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 15:13:41 -0500
  Subject: ET Life Or A Man On Mars?

  Source:
  http://tinyurl.com/269cuo
  Jan 23, 2008
  [Image here:
    http://tinyurl.com/2df9mm ]
  Is There Really Extraterrestrial Life Or A Man on Mars?
  By Leveling Truth
  The media world is buzzing about whether or not we are really
  alone in the universe after recent images from Mars surface give
  the appearance of a figure walking on the Red Planet.
  The photographs, which were taken four years ago, by NASA's Mars
  Explorer Spirit are sketchy and blurred images at best. Some
  outlets claim the figure looks like a woman with an outstretched
  arm, others say it resembles Bigfoot. Others claim it looks like
  a man walking, sitting, or pointing and some descriptions
  dismiss it entirely as just an oddly misshapen rock.
  Since the Rorschach Test for Extraterrestrial Life on Mars has
  already been so widely discussed, perhaps we can put our
  opinions aside and look at the real issues these photographs
  present:
  What is the real likelihood that there really is
  extraterrestrial life on Mars?
  Why is the possibility of life on Mars so important, right now?
  The possibility of life on Mars is not entirely a new concept as
  it has received a sizeable amount of news and press coverage,
  particularly in the last two decades.
  A press release date August 7, 1996 from NASA reported that a
  NASA research team discovered the first organic molecules
  thought to be of Martian origin within a meteorite, called
  ALH84001. The meteorite, found in Antarctica in 1984, supplied
  indirect evidence for the existence of microbial life found in
  several mineral features and possible microscopic fossils of
  primitive, bacteria-like organisms.
  Within the press release from NASA, planetary scientist Dr.
  David McKay, is quoted. "There is not any one finding that leads
  us to believe that this is evidence of past life on Mars.
  Rather, it is a combination of many things that we have found,"
  said McKay. McKay later adds that, "The relationship of all of
  these things in terms of location - within a few hundred
  thousandths of an inch of one another - is the most compelling
  evidence."

                                                       Georgina Bruni 1947 - 2008
  From: Nick Pope <contact.nul>
  Date: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 05:34:32 -0000
  Archived: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 07:19:15 -0500
  Subject: Georgina Bruni 1947 - 2008

  I am very sorry to have to report that Georgina Bruni died at
  the weekend, following a long illness which she fought with
  great courage and dignity.
  She led an extraordinary life and tried her hand at a wide
  variety of jobs, working variously as a dancer, fashion designer
  and nightclub manager. She travelled extensively and at various
  times lived in Jersey, Italy, Hong Kong and America, before
  settling in London in 1992. She wrote poetry, designed a
  positive thinking course and founded Hot Gossip, an online
  magazine. She was a former director of the Yacht Club, where she
  was involved in hosting social events for MPs, diplomats and MoD
  officials. Later on she became a PR consultant and ran a social
  club, Le Club 2000.
  Georgina is best known to this List for her research into the
  Rendlesham Forest incident. She consulted on and contributed to
  various TV documentaries on the subject and her book on the
  case, You Can't Tell The People, won her praise not just from
  the UFO community but from former Chief of the Defence Staff
  Lord Hill-Norton and from Gordon Williams, who had been
  Commanding Officer of the twin bases of Bentwaters and
  Woodbridge when the incident occurred.

  Best wishes,
  Nick Pope
  http://www.nickpope.net

  miles [69 statute miles] in diameter centered on the ranch.

  sightings areas.

                                                Area 51 Re-named 'Homey Airport'
  From: Jay Nelson <jnelson.nul>
  Date: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 12:38:57 -0700
  Archived: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 08:06:54 -0500
  Subject: Area 51 Re-named 'Homey Airport'
  -----
  Source: The Airforce Times - Reno, Nevada, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/2qbd2t
  Jan 23, 2008

  Area 51 Designated With A New Name
  By Philip Ewing - Staff writer
  The Air Force's classified test range at Groom Lake, Nev., has
  never lacked for evocative nicknames - it and its restricted
  airspace have been called Dreamland, Paradise Ranch, The Box
  and, most famously, Area 51. Now there's a less romantic moniker
  to throw on the pile: Homey Airport, according to a few civilian
  aviation journals.
  "Homey Airport" now appears as the official name for a certain
  air base near a certain dry lake bed in Nevada, according to
  reports in the Web site of the Aircraft Owners and Pilots
  Association, as well as the Daily Aviator blog and others. New
  editions of flight planning software and civilian aviators' GPS
  gear lists the name and the official designation KXTA - which
  online wags have speculated stands for 'extraterrestrial
  airport'. (The 'k' designation indicates only that the field is
  in the U.S., according to the Federal Aviation Administration.)
  Capt. Jessica Martin, a spokeswoman for Nellis Air Force Base,
  which sits 85 miles south of Homey Airport and is responsible
  for the airspace and any ground facilities, said that "we
  already know about the designation, but it doesn't have any
  effect on operations at the base."
  Martin said she didn't know the origin of the name Homey
  Airport.
  Featured in movies, TV shows and video games, Area 51 is likely
  the most famous top-secret facility in the world and a favorite
  component of UFO and military conspiracy theories.
  The Department of Defense didn't even acknowledge the base
  existed until 1994, when former base employees sued the
  government and claimed they'd been poisoned by hazardous
  materials used at the base for research into stealth technology.
  Although the base and its work have long been highly classified,
  many of the aircraft tested there through the years are publicly
  familiar: the U2 and SR-71 Blackbird spy planes and the F-117
  Nighthawk stealth fighter all flew first off the long runways
  and dry lakebeds at Groom Lake.
  Some enthusiasts believe that work continues there today on
  advanced aircraft - including unmanned aerial vehicles, high-
  speed reconnaissance craft and even high-altitude blimps -
  though alien conspiracy buffs also speculate that Area 51's
  high profile has forced officials to move much of the top-secret
  stuff to the Army's Dugway Proving Ground in Utah.

                                                  Re: A Letter To My Congressman
  From: Steven Kaeser <steve.nul>
  Date: Thu, 24 Jan 2008 15:25:19 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 08:18:01 -0500
  Subject: Re: A Letter To My Congressman

  >From: Franklin Fields <fields.nul>
  >To: ufoupdates.nul
  >Date: Wed, 23 Jan 2008 21:54:18 -0500 (EST)
  >Subject: A Letter To My Congressman
  >Below is a letter I sent to congress in hopes that some might
  >draft a similar letter. I borrowed some verbiage so feel free to
  >grab what may be useful.
  >-----
  <snip>
  This is an effort that I applaud, with an understanding that
  it's similar to shouting into the wind. I work at the U.S.
  House, and have held positions both with a Member (in DC and the
  District), and also with Committees, and letters such as this
  are often ignored.
  Part of the issue is the volume of mail that received, with most
  serious mail efforts resulting in thousands of letters per day
  per Member. These are often National in nature, and usually
  trigger a "buck", or generic, response written by a legislative
  aide. A few letters, no matter how well written or logical,
  won't be noticed if they don't deal with an issue of importance
  on that day. UFOs, or unknown craft in the skies, don't even hit
  the radar screen (so to speak).
  There was only on Congressman that I'm aware of who was able to
  use the UFO genre as a positive for his campaign, and that New
  Mexico Congressman passed away a few years ago of cancer. While
  some Members and Staff privately have a curiosity about the
  subject, the issues of the day prevail over all others and it's
  a never ending series of crisis moments for most of those in
  Washington these days.
  Politicians would get involved if thousands of letters are
  received monthly on this subject, but it would also have to
  outweigh the letters against the Iraq war or supporting some
  economic bail out. You have to also understand that there is a
  percentage of letters from people that are labeled as "kooks" by
  the staff, because of the content or format, or perhaps because
  they've met them in the District and know of them first hand. A
  Member of Congress rarely actually sees any mail sent in, and
  often it is answered in his name by Staff.
  If you really want to get your Congressman involved, you may
  have to meet with them when they come to the District and
  personally express your interest and concern.
  And just to add one more point... email is sometimes used to
  send message to your Member of Congress, but a hand written
  letter shows that you took time to compose it and will cause
  them to write back. That takes a little more time on their part
  than simply hitting the "Reply" button or adding your email
  address to a list being sent a response.

  Steve

Asteroid To Buzz Earth




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 25

                                                          Asteroid To Buzz Earth
  From: Sheryl Gottschall <gottscha.nul>
  Date: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 09:43:05 +1000
  Archived: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 14:38:57 -0500
  Subject: Asteroid To Buzz Earth

  Source: The Courier Mail - Australia
  http://tinyurl.com/2mhzpv
  Thursday, January 24, 2008

  Asteroid To Buzz Earth
  A huge asteroid will zoom past Earth next week and will be so
  close that amateur astronomers should be able to spot it,
  experts say. Measuring between 150m and 600m across, asteroid
  2007 TU24 would inflict devastating regional damage were it to
  hit Earth, but there is no risk of any collision, they said.
  It will pass on Tuesday and come to within 534,000km of the
  Earth at its closest point at 6.34pm Queensland time according
  to a Near Earth Object database compiled by the University of
  Pisa in Italy.
  "For a brief time the asteroid will be observable in dark and
  clear skies with amateur telescopes of three inches (7.5cm) or
  larger," NASA said on its NEO site.
  Asteroid 2007 TU24 will make the closest approach of any known
  potentially hazardous asteroid of this size or larger until
  2027, NASA said, adding that objects of this size come close to
  Earth about every five years or so on average.
  The rock was discovered only last October under a surveillance
  program run by the University of Arizona.
  According to the Minor Planet Centre of the Paris-based
  International Astronomical Union (IAU), the closest detected
  approach by an asteroid was on March 31, 2004, by 2004 FU162,
  which came within 6500km of Earth.
  The day after 2007 TU24's terrestrial flyby, asteroid 2007 WD5
  is expected to come within 26,000km of Mars, a distance that is
  less than a whisker in space terms.
  Asteroid 2007 WD5 ignited a brief surge of excitement among
  astronomers after it was discovered in November. Initial
  computations of its orbit gave a roughly 1-in-25 chance that it
  might whack into Mars on January 30, providing a celestial show
  that could be monitored by US and European scoutcraft there.
  Measuring about 50m across, it would have delivered an impact
  equivalent to a three-megaton nuclear weapon.
  A rock of this size exploded in the atmosphere over Tunguska,
  Siberia, in 1908, felling around 80 million trees over 2200 sq
   km. But further calculation showed that the big splat would be
  a big miss. "It's highly unlikely that it's going to hit," said
  NEO expert Benny Peiser of Liverpool John Moores University in
  northwestern England, as the odds of a collision by 2007 WD5
  fell to around 0.01 per cent, or one in 10,000.

                                            Follow-Up On Guanica Puerto Rico UFO
  From: Scott Corrales <lornis1.nul>
  Date: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 05:59:47 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 14:51:02 -0500
  Subject: Follow-Up On Guanica Puerto Rico UFO

  The Journal of Hispanic Ufology
  January 25, 2008
  Source: Argus-PR
  Date: Saturday, January 19, 2008
  PUERTO RICO: FOLLOW-UP on the Gu=E1nica UFO
  A Report from Jose A. Martinez
  We are continuing our report on the sightings of strange lights
  over the town of Guanica which have been taking place since last
  Friday. The sightings are ongoing. The day after having reported
  on the huge, classical saucer-shaped UFO, more detailed
  information was received from another district near the previous
  one (Vivones).This time the report came from Puig, near the town
  of Guanica. Behind this district we find the notorious Lajas
  Valley. Several witnesses reported seeing a strange light,
  bright orange in color, appear out of nowhere at low altitude
  close to them. This luminous phenomenon did not make any noise
  or perceptible sounds. This incident took place at an early time
  - 8:10 p.m. - and the objects maneuvers were a zig-zag in the
  same location very low altitude before taking off toward Lajas
  at an incredible speed. Jose Hernandez is not a believer in
  UFOs and says that he had never seen one in his life until that
  evening, and cannot explain what he saw with his own eyes. His
  brother in law added that he nad never seen anything like it
  either, and that he was impressed to see this object such a
  short distance away from them.
  Two Police Officers from Guanica Report UFO on Guanica Back Road
  Toward Lajas
  Source: Argus PR
  Date: Sunday, January 20, 2008
  Two municipal policemen on their day off were spending time with
  their families at La Parguera, Lajas. (The officers' names will
  not be disclosed at their request). When both families departed
  the La Parguera district, they made ready to return to Guanica
  using a back road known as Los Hornos, a lonely road that runs
  from Ensenada de Guanica to Parguera - deserted and without
  electric lighting except for some intersections and the odd
  house.
  Taking advantage of the darkness, one of the officer pulled over
  to urinate. When this physiological imperative was nearly over,
  he noticed that there was on object nearby - hovering at low
  altitude and perfectly dark. Frightened, he ran back to his car.
  The object suddenly turned on its lights and followed them all
  the way back to Ensenada de Guanica. The object stopped
  following them once they reached the area that has good public
  lighting.
  ---
  Translation (c) 2008, S. Corrales, IHU
  Special thanks to Jose A. Martinez

  Of the many thousands of images of UFOs in the public domain,
  with hundreds more images being added every year thanks partly
  to the wide use of cell phones with cameras, most ufologists
  still consider the Trindada Island images to be among the top
  five examples of physical evidence that support the very popular
  belief that some UFOs are indeed structured ("nuts and bolts")
  objects very different to the known aerial craft manufactured
  here on Earth and thus must be of extraterrestrial origin.
  If there is now reasonable doubt, not necessarily proof, that
  these UFO pictures taken by Almiro Barauna are fakes, this alone
  could be enough to sway the ufological jury to reconsider all
  other credible photographic/video evidence we as our basis for
  the popular belief that one of the explanations for UFOs are ET
  craft. This reason alone can explain why none of the defenders
  of this case chose to remain silent about this very important
  revelation by Brazilian researcher Rodolpho Gauthier and even to
  my post on the UFO UpDates list (Re: Mobile Phone Images?, Sat.,
  19 January 2008) where I made mention of the Trinidad (sic)
  Island UFO pictures when discussing the actual but unknowable
  percentage of UFO pictures that are faked.
  The very large number of hoaxed UFO pictures and fake/dubious

  Hello John & List
  I don't know when the contents of the Mundo Illustrado article
  were in contention here. Not, as far as I recall, during my own
  List exchanges with Mori and others, but perhaps at some other
  time? Well, for my own part I have corresponded with Mori off-
  List about it, but it's actually very hard to get focused,
  substantive discussion on nitty-gritty case details going on-
  List, as my recent largely-futile attempts with Rendlesham have
  proved, so I left it alone. Now that you've raised it again,
  however, let's have a go.
  I think I'm representing Mori correctly thus: The content
  revealed, particularly the images, is new circumstantial
  evidence of a hoax by Barauna, significant new evidence, because
  the "classic inclined Saturn shape" (or repeated variations on
  this phrase) of the model used, and the resemblance of a beach
  scene to the Trindade photos ("very similar"), constitute a
  "cosmic coincidence" or an "extraordinary coincidence". So
  "extremely similar" is the Trindade object to this "classic
  (roughly) Saturn-shaped flying saucer inclined" that, Mori
  suggests, "It's actually possible, with some distortion, that
  this model could have created the image of the Trindade saucer."
  Now I should say that the work of Mori and Rodolpho Gauthier is
  laudable in getting this famous Lima article copied and
  publicised. It is very interesting and valuable to finally see
  it in all its glory, even though the text and general nature of
  the photos have been well known for many years. The photos are
  in fact very much as they were described to me by another
  researcher (well-known on this List) a couple of years ago, who
  had seen a copy but was unwillingly constrained from
  distributing it by associates who felt they owned the right to
  control that copy. They never have published it, and Mori is
  absolutely in the right to be critical of them. So I am
  interested at last to see the model "UFO" which was described to
  me as looking rather like "tap washers" hanging on a thread.
  This turns out to have been pretty accurate.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m26-002.shtml[09/12/2011 23:54:01]
Re: 'How To Fake UFO Photos' By Almiro Barauna


  In case anyone is in any doubt, we should explain that this
  little 1954 article is not news. The text of it has been a
  subject of discussion for years. I myself have corresponded with
  Mori in pedantic detail about the meaning of words and phrases
  in it. It has been known since 1958. It was discussed in the
  Brazilian press in 1958. No one, including Barauna, has ever
  made any secret of it so far as I am aware (except perhaps the
  ufologists mentioned above). US Naval Attache Capt Sunderland's
  1958 report alludes to it by title and content. It wasn't the
  only thing either - Barauna had published other "fun" features
  demonstrating "trick" photography such as treasure chests under
  the sea and so on. He obviously enjoyed such stuff - as would
  most photographers, which is why the professional-quality
  Rollieflex he used was manufactured deliberately with the
  facility to make double exposures for exactly that reason. He
  was rather well known for it.
  So we knew that Barauna had made some spoof double-exposure UFO
  photos for Mundo Illustrado four years before. We knew that he'd
  used (or, strictly speaking, he and Lima had used - at Lima's
  house, and demonstrated apparently by Lima's wife) a little
  suspended model made of "chips of the Carioca fleet" which we
  were able to infer (but not prove, despite Mori's local
  knowledge) must have been some sort of local transport token. We
  also knew (a fact not made explicit in the article incidentally)
  that at least part of the motivation was to debunk the famous
  Barra da Tijuca hoax of 1952 involving Joao Martins (who was to
  have a part to play in Barauna's Trindade photos of 1958 as an
  interviewing reporter!). We knew all this. What more, then, do
  we know now?
  We now have a slightly better idea of what the famous "chips of
  the Carioca Fleet" looked like. The article does not make their
  nature any clearer (as far as I can tell) but it is clear that
  they have one flat face, and apparently a flat raised boss on
  the other face around a central hole. Looking at the "close-up"
  of the assembled UFO with two flat faces glued together, the
  shape of each chip appears to be like a large washer with a
  smaller washer glued on one side. This is quite a strange
  construction for a bus token, but is simple and presumably cheap
  to produce. It would be surprising if such a thing had a still
  more complicated shape than this, such as having a curved dome
  on one side. Why would it? And the photo does not show any sign
  of such a thing. The double Carioca chip is not actually "Saturn
  shaped". It is effectively a stack of four flat discs.
  So I certainly do not see a model that could have been used for
  the Trindade photos, with or without "distortion". There is a
  resemblance to the flat object with flat annular bosses top and
  bottom in the 1952 Keffel photos (Barra da Tijuca).
  But anyway, it is true that the glued Carioca chips do make a
  disc with a raised central area top and bottom so that
  (neglecting the knot of the thread) there is symmetry on the
  rotational axis normal to the plane of the disc. One can
  certainly argue that this is a coincidence with the Trindade
  object, but it is a coincidence shared by numerous other claimed
  lenticular saucer types with symmetry on that axis. There is no
  direct connection with the Trindade object, and IMO to try and
  inflate the inaccurate claim that this evidently washer-like
  object is "Saturn shaped" by further claiming significance for
  the fact that it is tilted away from the horizontal ("classic
  inclined Saturn shape") is reaching a little far.
  So what do we know that we did not know years ago? Honestly,
  nothing. The existence of this article and its spoof UFO photos,
  and the fact that Barauna had published trick photos of various
  other kinds, were well known since 1958. If some real direct
  connection could have been made with the Trindade photos then
  that would have been very interesting indeed. But in all
  conscience I could see no such connection, and said so to Mori.
  Mori's reply conceded that we did indeed already know these
  things, that there was nothing conclusive in the Lima article,
  but still claimed that it "adds to the circumstantial evidence
  of hoax. One must admit it's quite an extraordinary coincidence
  that Barauna hoaxed these photos, which also feature a model of
  a classic (roughly) Saturn-shaped flying saucer inclined."
  I still didn't follow this reasoning. We knew there were photos


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m26-002.shtml[09/12/2011 23:54:01]
Re: 'How To Fake UFO Photos' By Almiro Barauna

  of a model saucer made of "Carioca chips", we knew therefore
  that it would be a disc(oid), and we knew that it was
  photographed hanging on a thread. I wonder what shape,
  consistent with this, it would need to have had in order for us
  to have said "Well, that doesn't support the hoax theory"? Would
  a flat disc with a proper dome on one side (potentially
  transformable into a true Trindade "Saturn" by glueing two
  together) have been a less significant find than what we have -
   a flat disc with smaller flat discs on both sides, which is not
  transformable into a domed shape by any operation?
  I suspect that almost any likely saucer shape we had found in
  these photos could be connected with Trindade by an equally
  inconclusive argument.
  And if the "inclined" angle the Lima model happens to be hanging
  at is significant because it is similar to one of the Trindade
  photos (a suggestion repeatedly made by Mori and illustrated on
  his webpage by a comparison enlargement with the3rd Trindade
  image), then it must be the case - surely? - that there are
  other inclinations that would not have been significant. But
  what angle would it have to have been inclined at for us to
  conclude "The inclinations of the two discs are significantly
  different and argue _against_ a hoax"? I can't imagine Mori or
  anyone saying such a thing, because this is an arbitrary
  variable on any theory whatever, including both suspended models
  and flying machines.
  And in fact in three of the four Trindade photos the inclination
  is much nearer the horizontal. If the Lima model had been
  hanging almost horizontally we would have been able to say, with
  _more_ force, "Look, the inclination is similar in 75% of the
  photos!" But of course the inclination in the Lima photos
  depends on the fact that the suspension point is not central,
  owing to the Polo-holes in the Carioca chips. The shape of the
  Trindade object, which clearly is not made of holey Carioca
  chips, does not appear to have this constraint, and the point of
  attachment of a hypothetical thread is again a free variable.
  There is no necessary or even likely causal connection in the
  two cases.
  What about Mori's argument that one of the Lima photos showing a
  beach is very similar to the Trindade ones?
  I'm afraid I can't see this either. At least two of the three
  photos (possibly all three) are taken over the coast. Barauna
  lived and worked on the coast, Niteroi if I remember rightly. He
  was interested in the sea, sea photography, subaqua. Most of the
  landscape photos of his that I have seen are taken on the coast.
  This is not surprising, I suppose most of the population of
  Brazil lives and travels near the coast. But Mori claims that
  one of these three photos is "very similar" to the Trindade ones
  in some more significant way. Beyond the fact that one photo is
  taken in daylight I am unable to see what Mori means and I
  believe he would have difficulty justifying this impression
  objectively. That photo shows a fat smudge of light trailing
  across the sky (simple double exposure of the torch-lit Carioca
  UFO swinging on a thread) above a rural coastal scene.
  So I think that in respect of the shape, and the orientation,
  and the location, Mori is seeing things that resonate
  satisfyingly with his pre-conception (honourably arrived at, I
  do not dispute) of hoax. But I don't think that seeing these
  photos offers any truly new evidence of anything. They do of
  course illustrate graphically what we already knew textually and
  by repute: That Barauna was a well-known and practiced semi-
  professional photographer who knew his way around an expensive
  Rolleiflex and a darkroom. The Trindade photos, whatever their
  explanation, are (as I can attest from having closely examined
  some excellents scans) remarkably rich in detail and information
  that give us quite a bit to chew on. A couple of blurred snaps
  by a poorly-equipped photographic novice wouldn't have kept us
  all
  interested for so long.

  Martin Shough

  Don,
  France has always been a quasi-member of NATO/OTAN. Their
  military participation ended when France's government kicked out
  the NATO Headquarters in 1967. The source below points out that
  the French military is not integrated with the NATO chain of
  command.
  See:
  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO
  My personal observation comes from my assignment to Allied
  Forces South (AFSOUTH) in Naples, Italy from January 1977 to
  January 1980. One of our customers in the communications center
  was the FMM (French Military Mission). I had almost daily
  contact with FMM staff including the French admiral in charge.
  The FMM by NATO agreement were to use only our communications
  center; however, one day we received a service message from a
  French Navy base, I think Marseilles, requesting status on a
  specific communications circuit or channel. I didn't read French
  very well but recognized this service message would be of
  interest to Admiral Shear's staff. I wrote a short note on the
  service message and sent it to the command center. Bottom line:
  the French admiral and staff were chastised and admonished for
  establishing a communications circuit through the Italian postal
  and telegraph service.
  I remember sending and receiving messages to several French
  military commands and activities including the French aircraft
  carrier, FS FOCH.

  Terry

History & Sci Fi Channels Debut Dueling 'UFO




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 26

                                       History & Sci Fi Channels Debut Dueling 'UFO
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Sat, 26 Jan 2008 19:19:23 -0500
  Archived: Sat, 26 Jan 2008 19:19:23 -0500
  Subject: History & Sci Fi Channels Debut Dueling 'UFO



  Source: Reality TV World - Mansfield, Massachusetts, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/3dsxat
  01/25/2008

  History & Sci Fi Channels Debut Dueling 'UFO Hunters' Feb 6.
  By Christopher Rocchio and Steve Rogers
  In what appears to be an unprecedented scenario, both networks
  are currently planning to premiere different reality programs
  with the same name and the same subject matter on the same night
  in the same time period.
  The History Channel's UFO Hunters will follow a team from UFO
  Magazine as they investigate UFO cases in North America and
  Europe while Sci Fi Channel's UFO Hunters will follow a team
  from the New York Strange Phenomena Investigators organization
  investigating their own set of UFO cases. Both shows are
  currently scheduled to premiere Wednesday, February 6 at 10PM
  ET/PT.
  F. Jay Dougherty, a professor of law at Loyola Law School Los
  Angeles who spoke with Reality TV World on Friday, said
  television program titles aren't copyrightable but can obtain
  trademark protection -- a move that, rather than just selecting
  an alternative name, both shows are attempting.
  "Normally, the competitive process would have weeded it out,"
  said Dougherty. "You tend to work these things out through
  changing names, or changing release dates. Normally they kind
  of work out in the process of relationships in the commercial
  world. I'm a little surprised that they're butting heads like
  this."
  The History Channel, which is billing its program as a "a
  spinoff from the network's hit program 'UFO Hunters' which
  premiered in 2005," filed a United States Patent and Trademark
  Office application to trademark the use of the term "UFO
  Hunters" in "entertainment services, including an on-going
  television series featuring stories about the paranormal,
  aliens, and unusual phenomena" as well as "pre-recorded audio
  and video tapes and discs" on October 31, 2007.
  The application, formally filed by A&E Television Networks, The
  History Channel's corporate parent, was filed under the "use in
  commerce" basis -- a status used in cases in which the filer is
  claiming to have already used the term they are attempting to
  trademark.
  The History Channel's UFO Hunters series is being produced by
  Motion Picture Production, Inc., the same production company
  that produced UFO Files, an anthology documentary television
  series that premiered on the network in 2004.
  In July 2005, The History Channel premiered a UFO Files episode


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m26-010.shtml[09/12/2011 23:54:06]
History & Sci Fi Channels Debut Dueling 'UFO

  entitled "UFO Hunters." The DVD edition of the one-hour
  episode, listed as "UFO Files: UFO Hunters DVD," is currently
  available for purchase on A&E's website. Schedule information
  available on The History Channel's website also lists an
  upcoming February 2 rebroadcast of the program as UFO Files: UFO
  Hunters and shows "UFO Files" as the show's title and "UFO
  Hunters" as the episode's title.
  Sci Fi Channel, which originally announced it had ordered a new
  UFO Hunters reality series produced by the producers of its
  popular Ghost Hunters reality series last July, filed its
  trademark application less than a week after The History
  Channel's filing.
  The application, filed on November 5, 2007 by Pilgrim Films and
  Television, the production company behind both Ghost Hunters and
  UFO Hunters, attempts to trademark the use of the term "UFO
  Hunters" with regard to "entertainment services in the nature of
  an on-going reality-based television program," as well as in
  websites and fan clubs. Since it isn't claiming any prior use
  of the term, Pilgrim's "UFO Hunters" request was filed under the
  "intent to use" basis.
  So far, neither trademark application has been assigned an
  examiner or advanced beyond the initial filing stage -- an
  unsurprising development given the approval process can take
  several years.
  At first glance, its earlier filing status and (albeit
  potentially questionable) history of previous use might appear
  to give The History Channel a stronger case, but that doesn't
  necessarily mean the network's claim will eventually be granted.
  According to Dougherty, it could be difficult for either The
  History Channel or Sci Fi Channel to obtain trademark rights
  since the UFO Hunters title is a "fairly weak" trademark due to
  it's "descriptive" title.
  "UFO Hunters is a more imaginative title for a work," said
  Dougherty. "In other words, it's kind of descriptive what the
  show's about. I think courts are a little bit reluctant to make
  it difficult to use words in a descriptive way. When you use
  words that are descriptive, it makes it harder for you to get
  exclusive trademark rights in those words."
  Nor is the fact that The History Channel is already displaying a
  "TM" mark alongside its UFO Hunters title an indication of any
  already-granted rights.
  "Anybody can put a 'TM' next to anything that they intend to
  trademark," Dougherty explained. "[It just indicates] that you
  are intending to use the title as a trademark."
  When contacted by Reality TV World earlier this week, both
  networks acknowledged being aware of the other network's program
  but stated they were not aware of any plans to change their own
  program's title. However according to a Sci Fi Channel
  spokesperson reached Friday, the network has not currently
  scheduled any additional UFO Hunters broadcasts beyond the
  February 6 broadcast of the show's pilot episode.
  Somewhat ironically, both the Sci Fi Channel and The History
  Channel share some common corporate ownership. Sci Fi Channel
  is owned by NBC Universal while A&E Television Networks is a
  joint venture between The Hearst Corporation, ABC Inc., and NBC
  Universal.
  While UFO Hunters doesn't represent the first time networks have
  dueled with similar reality show concepts, it is certainly the
  most extreme case.
  <snip>

Buried Memories?




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Jan > Jan 26

                                                              Buried Memories?
  From: John Dowler <jdowler.nul>
  Date: Fri, 25 Jan 2008 22:16:55 -0800
  Archived: Sat, 26 Jan 2008 19:37:15 -0500
  Subject: Buried Memories?

  In the early nineties I interviewed several abductees and
  contactees who were traumatized by experiences with UFO
  phenomena. Several asked me to arrange hypnotic regression to
  access hidden memories. More than a couple found it very
  difficult to cope.
  In the same period stories were coming forward of people
  discovering incest and other abuse in their past through a
  similar technique. Some brought charges against their parents
  and destroyed their reputations, and people went to jail. Later
  it emerged that in some of these cases, the victims later
  changed their minds or new evidence came out rendering their
  testimony under hypnosis highly suspect. There was never an
  answer to why they had experienced these intense new memories so
  strongly that their families were destroyed if they 'simply
  weren't true'.
  I resisted getting involved with hypnosis. I felt and still do
  that it's a very effective way to pry up the rock, but not
  necessarily to deal with the creatures that crawl out, whether
  real or false.
  This was about a decade ago, and I drifted away from the
  subject. Now I'm wondering about those victims who decided
  they'd suffered the ultimate betrayal, then the realization that
  they were wrong about their parents. I don't know why it never
  occured to me before because I actually had a friend who
  discovered buried memories of what she took to be incest and
  humiliating 'sharing with friends' as a child.
  Has anyone investigated whether the intense sexual trauma the
  victims reported was not from their parents but from pearheads
  in saucers? So not incest, but possibly a family affair?
  Of course after all they've been through, they might not want to
  pry up the rock again.

  John Dowler

                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena

                                                           'Demons In The Dark'
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Sat, 26 Jan 2008 19:57:39 -0500
  Archived: Sat, 26 Jan 2008 19:57:39 -0500
  Subject: 'Demons In The Dark'



  Source: Newsweek Magazine - New York, USA
  http://www.newsweek.com/id/96014/
  Jan 18, 2008

  'Demons In The Dark'
  How scientists talk about UFO sightings.
  Newsweek Web Exclusive

  On an otherwise unremarkable January night in Stephenville,
  Texas, dozens of people looked to the sky and saw a vast vessel
  with a combination of red, white and yellow lights flying fast
  over the area's farms. One observer said the vessel was a mile
  long. Several said they saw fighter jets chasing it. One said he
  feared the object's appearance might mean "the end of times."
  A pilot, a cop and some businessmen, housewives, and children
  all say they saw a UFO on Jan. 8. The spaceship moved over the
  area for several seconds, witnesses said, and then zoomed away
  300 times faster than a Cessna jet can travel.
  UFO sightings make the news several times a year. In 2007 eight
  such episodes attracted headlines. Most sightings take place in
  the South and West.
  UFO spotters endure endless jokes about their experiences. But
  even people who debunk the very notion of UFOs take them
  seriously. "No one should make fun" of Stephenville's UFO
  spotters, says Theodore Schick of Muhlenberg College, a liberal
  arts school in Allentown, Pa. They "had a real experience that's
  out of the ordinary." But Schick and experts in physics and
  human psychology say the experiences have scientific
  explanations. Scientists now probe the most microscopic aspects
  of the brain and the farthest reaches of the galaxy.
  Evolution provides a good starting place for explaining why
  people have paranormal experiences.
  For all but the last 10,000 years of human history, man survived
  by hunting and gathering plants. To interpret a mysterious
  world, man projected his own fears and understandings onto his
  environment. In the "enchanted" view of the world, every part of
  nature=97rocks, trees, hills, water=97was alive and filled with
  spirit. Even in the age of science, the human brain still
  projects ideas and images on the world.
  "People have been seeing things long before they ever had any
  ideas about UFOs," says Robert Park, a physicist at the
  University of Maryland. "In the Middle Ages we saw demons in the
  dark. At other times we see angels in the things we can't
  explain."
  When people see something they cannot explain=97which might happen


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m26-019.shtml[09/12/2011 23:54:11]
'Demons In The Dark'

  more frequently in a "noisy environment," Park says=97they use
  images stored in the brain to complete the picture and make
  sense of it. Because culture is full of images from "The
  Twilight Zone," "Close Encounters of the Third Kind," "The
  Matrix," and UFO documentaries on the Discovery Channel, people
  project those sci-fi images.
  People seeing images also make precise assessments that defy
  easy explanation. A Stephenville businessman's estimate that a
  milelong spaceship was traveling 120,000 miles an hour=97he says
  the ship moved as fast in four seconds as his Cessna jet travels
  in 20 minutes=97exceeds the average person's ability to judge
  distances and speed.
  The Austrian philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein used the image of
  the "duck-rabbit" to explain how people construct ideas and
  images according to the language of their culture. The image
  could be viewed as either a duck or a rabbit. Studies show that
  some people are able to see one of the figures while others can
  see both. How each person interprets the image depends on both
  psychological and social factors.
  Michael Persinger, a behavioral neuroscientist at Laurentian
  University, takes the analysis of brainwork even deeper. Working
  with 2,000 research subjects, Persinger has shown how magnetic
  stimulation of different parts of the brain can activate
  different feelings and emotions=97such as oneness with God,
  feelings of love and lust, anger and anxiety, and even the
  feeling of being in the presence of a UFO.
  Many UFO sightings come during a period of earthquakes, when
  shifts in the earth's plates alter the atmosphere's magnetic
  charges. So it's not surprising that people's brains could
  vividly experience what seems to be a UFO sighting or even an
  alien abduction.
  (In one famous encounter, Persinger tried to induce a religious
  experience in the mind of atheist Richard Dawkins. Alas, Dawkins
  apparently has a low level of temporal-lobe sensitivity, so his
  brain did not react as much as others=92) to the magnetic
  stimulation.
  Simple physics, scientists say, makes intergalactic space travel
  close to impossible. An international research team studied
  whether teleporting people=97that is, transporting them by
  transmitting information about their composition, like sending a
  fax=97is possible. The answer is yes, but it would require 100
  million centuries to transfer the data of
  100,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 bits. "It would be
  easier to walk," cracks Samuel Braunstein, a computer science
  professor at the University of York.
  Proving the absence of something is always harder than proving
  the presence of something, so the UFO sightings continue. "You
  cannot disprove a negative," says Park, the author of "Voodoo
  Science: The Road From Foolishness to Fraud," a tour of various
  forms of questionable "scientific" beliefs. "You can't prove
  that there wasn't a UFO." The best anyone can do, says Schick,
  is gather facts and see what theory best fits those facts. "You
  have to compare the UFO explanation to other explanations," he
  says.
  The mirror image of the belief in UFOs is disbelief in historic
  events, like the moon landing. Carl Everett, a one-time All-Star
  baseball player with the Boston Red Sox, evoked hoots in 2000
  when he told Sports Illustrated, "Yeah, that could have
  happened. It's possible. That is something you could prove. You
  can't prove dinosaurs ever existed. I feel it's far-fetched."
  Scientists defend UFO believers against charges that they're
  psychologically deranged. People who report UFO sightings and
  abductions, a 1993 study in the Journal of Abnormal Psychology
  concluded, are just as intelligent, psychologically healthy, and
  free of fantasies as people without such experiences. People
  with UFO experiences differed on only one known measure: sleep
  deprivation.
  The problem is not that UFO sighters are imbalanced, some
  scientists say, but rather that they do not scrutinize their
  experiences adequately=97which is often hard to do, because the
  environment is filled with mysterious phenomena. "How many


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/jan/m26-019.shtml[09/12/2011 23:54:11]
'Demons In The Dark'

  people know about stealth bombers being escorted by fighter
  jets?" asks Michael Shermer, the author of "Why People Believe
  Weird Things." "I have to say, it's the spookiest thing I've
  ever seen. Maybe that's what they saw [in Stephenville]."
  Shermer briefly believed in UFOs himself. While cycling on the
  3,000-mile Race Across America in 1983, he thought he was about
  to be abducted. "I went hours without sleep and thought my crew
  members were aliens trying to abduct me and [the support
  vehicle] was a spaceship," he says. "That made me realize that
  when people had an experience, they really had something
  meaningful happen. The question is, what does that mean?"
  The University of Maryland's Park recalls a more mundane
  experience more than 50 years ago. Stationed in Roswell, N.M.,
  in 1954, he was driving home on a desolate road one night after
  visiting his parents in Texas. He saw a streak of green-blue
  light, which he recognized as the glow of an ice meteorite.
  Then, subconsciously primed for a paranormal experience, he
  believed for a few seconds that he witnessed a UFO.
  "I saw a brilliant light going across the sky on a road," he
  says. "It looked like a disc to me. When I accelerated, the
  thing sped up with me. I thought something was going on. I
  slammed on the brakes=97and it was the reflection of my headlights
  on the telephone lines."
  With that, Park learned the ultimate lesson for a scientist:
  humility.

  Euchner, a lecturer in English at Yale University, is completing
  a book about suicide at the Golden Gate Bridge.

  >Brazilian press in 1958. No one, including Barauna, has ever

  >ufologists mentioned above). US Naval Attache Capt Sunderland's
  >1958 report alludes to it by title and content. It wasn't the
